bugs.name: Actinomyces israelii
bugs.symptoms: Lumpy jaw with draining sinus tracts; yellow sulfur granules

bugs.name: Anaplasma phagocytophilum
bugs.symptoms: Fever, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia; morulae in neutrophils

bugs.name: Aspergillus fumigatus
bugs.symptoms: Halo sign on chest CT in neutropenia; positive galactomannan

bugs.name: Babesia microti
bugs.symptoms: Hemolytic anemia and fever; Maltese cross tetrads on smear; severe in asplenics
bugs.treatment: Atovaquone plus azithromycin (moderate); clindamycin plus quinine (severe)

bugs.name: Bacillus anthracis
bugs.symptoms: Painless black eschar with edema; mediastinal widening in inhalation form
bugs.treatment: Ciprofloxacin or doxycycline plus additional agents

bugs.name: Bartonella bacilliformis
bugs.symptoms: Acute severe hemolytic anemia then chronic blood-filled Peruvian Warts; spread by sandfly
bugs.treatment: Oroya fever: ciprofloxacin plus ceftriaxone; verruga peruana: rifampin or streptomycin

bugs.name: Bartonella henselae
bugs.symptoms: Papule at scratch site then painful regional lymphadenopathy; bacillary angiomatosis in AIDS

bugs.name: Bartonella quintana
bugs.symptoms: Relapsing fever every 5 days with severe shin and back pain; spread by body lice

bugs.name: Borrelia burgdorferi
bugs.symptoms: Erythema migrans bull's-eye rash; AV block, Bell's palsy, Lyme arthritis

bugs.name: Borrelia recurrentis
bugs.geography: Refugee camps, war zones (Ethiopia, Eritrea, Sudan, Somalia)
bugs.symptoms: Recurrent febrile episodes from antigenic variation

bugs.name: Brucella melitensis
bugs.geography: Mediterranean, Middle East, Latin America, Africa, West Asia
bugs.symptoms: Undulant fevers, night sweats, back pain; from unpasteurized dairy

bugs.name: Candida albicans
bugs.symptoms: Oral thrush, esophageal/vaginal candidiasis; bloodstream infection
bugs.treatment: Echinocandin for candidemia; fluconazole for mucosal disease

bugs.name: Clostridioides difficile
bugs.symptoms: Watery diarrhea after broad-spectrum antibiotic use disrupts microbiome

bugs.name: Corynebacterium minutissimum
bugs.symptoms: Brown intertriginous patches; coral-red fluorescence on Wood's lamp

bugs.name: Coxiella burnetii
bugs.symptoms: Atypical pneumonia and granulomatous hepatitis; culture-negative endocarditis
bugs.treatment: Doxycycline; add hydroxychloroquine for chronic endocarditis

bugs.name: Coxsackievirus A16
bugs.symptoms: Painful oral ulcers plus vesicles on palms, soles, and buttocks

bugs.name: Cryptococcus neoformans
bugs.symptoms: Headache with high intracranial pressure; encapsulated yeast on India ink
bugs.treatment: Liposomal amphotericin B plus flucytosine; then oral fluconazole; serial LPs for pressure

bugs.name: Cutibacterium acnes
bugs.symptoms: Inflammatory comedones; gram-positive aerotolerant rod

bugs.name: Cytomegalovirus (CMV)
bugs.symptoms: Pizza-pie retina (hemorrhage plus exudates); deep linear esophageal ulcers; CD4 < 50

bugs.name: Dengue virus
bugs.symptoms: Breakbone fever; second infection worsened by antibody-dependent enhancement

bugs.name: Ebola virus
bugs.symptoms: Cytokine storm, vascular leak, DIC, hypovolemic shock; 50-90% mortality

bugs.name: Ehrlichia chaffeensis
bugs.symptoms: Fever, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia; morulae in monocytes

bugs.name: Entamoeba histolytica
bugs.symptoms: Bloody diarrhea; RUQ pain with 'anchovy paste' liver abscess

bugs.name: Francisella tularensis
bugs.symptoms: Ulceroglandular: skin ulcer with regional lymphadenopathy; very low infectious dose
bugs.treatment: Gentamicin (drug of choice); alternatives: doxycycline, ciprofloxacin

bugs.name: Giardia lamblia
bugs.symptoms: Foul-smelling, fatty, non-bloody diarrhea and bloating

bugs.name: Hantavirus (Sin Nombre virus)
bugs.symptoms: Flu-like prodrome (fever, chills, headache, nausea, back pain); progresses to hypotension, vascular leakage, acute kidney failure; rodent droppings exposure

bugs.name: Herpes simplex virus
bugs.symptoms: Recurrent grouped vesicles on erythematous base; prodromal tingling

bugs.name: HIV (Human Immunodeficiency Virus)
bugs.symptoms: Acute retroviral syndrome then CD4 decline below 200 with opportunistic infections

bugs.name: HTLV-1
bugs.geography: Japan, Caribbean, Central/South America, and parts of Africa
bugs.symptoms: ATLL (cutaneous lesions, lytic bone lesions, hypercalcemia); tropical spastic paraparesis
bugs.treatment: No effective antiretroviral therapy prevents ATLL

bugs.name: Human herpesvirus 6
bugs.symptoms: High fever 3-5 days then rash appears as fever defervesces

bugs.name: JC virus
bugs.symptoms: Subacute cognitive decline; non-enhancing white matter lesions on MRI
bugs.treatment: No specific therapy; restore immunity with ART

bugs.name: Lassa virus
bugs.symptoms: Often mild febrile illness; sensorineural deafness in one-third of survivors

bugs.name: Leishmania braziliensis
bugs.symptoms: Disfiguring nasal and oropharyngeal mucosal destruction
bugs.treatment: Liposomal amphotericin B or pentavalent antimonials

bugs.name: Leishmania donovani
bugs.symptoms: Fever, weight loss, hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia; fatal if untreated

bugs.name: Leptospira interrogans
bugs.geography: Tropical regions; Hawaii in the US
bugs.symptoms: Calf myalgias, conjunctival suffusion; jaundice and AKI in Weil disease

bugs.name: Malassezia furfur
bugs.symptoms: Hypo/hyperpigmented trunk macules; spaghetti-and-meatballs on KOH
bugs.treatment: Selenium sulfide shampoo or topical antifungals

bugs.name: Marburg virus
bugs.symptoms: Cytokine storm with vascular leak and hemorrhage; fruit bat reservoir

bugs.name: Measles virus
bugs.symptoms: Cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots; cephalocaudal rash
bugs.treatment: Supportive; vitamin A; ribavirin; MMR for prevention

bugs.name: Molluscum contagiosum virus
bugs.symptoms: Discrete flesh-colored dome-shaped papules with central umbilication
bugs.treatment: Self-resolving; curettage, topicals, or light therapy if treated

bugs.name: Monkeypox virus
bugs.symptoms: Centripetal rash including palms/soles; all lesions at same stage

bugs.name: Mucorales
bugs.symptoms: Rhino-orbital-cerebral invasion in diabetic ketoacidosis and transplant patients
bugs.treatment: Liposomal amphotericin B plus emergent surgical debridement

bugs.name: Mycobacterium avium complex
bugs.symptoms: High fevers, night sweats, elevated alkaline phosphatase; CD4 < 50

bugs.name: Mycobacterium ulcerans
bugs.symptoms: Painless slowly enlarging skin ulcer with undermined edges

bugs.name: Neisseria meningitidis
bugs.geography: Worldwide; outbreaks in crowded living (prisons, dorms)
bugs.symptoms: Fever, neck stiffness, altered mentation, petechial/purpuric rash

bugs.name: Parvovirus B19
bugs.symptoms: Slapped-cheek rash, lacy reticular trunk rash; aplastic crisis, hydrops fetalis
bugs.treatment: Supportive; IVIG or intrauterine transfusion in at-risk groups

bugs.name: Plasmodium falciparum
bugs.geography: Sub-Saharan Africa, South America, Southeast Asia, India - most widespread and deadliest malaria parasite
bugs.symptoms: Irregular fever, RBC knobs causing capillary sequestration, coma, organ failure

bugs.name: Plasmodium malariae
bugs.symptoms: 72-hour quartan fever cycle; no hypnozoites

bugs.name: Plasmodium ovale
bugs.symptoms: 48-hour fever cycle; dormant liver hypnozoites causing relapse
bugs.treatment: Chloroquine plus primaquine or tafenoquine for radical cure

bugs.name: Plasmodium vivax
bugs.geography: Asia, Latin America, some parts of Africa
bugs.symptoms: 48-hour fever cycle; dormant liver hypnozoites causing relapse months later
bugs.treatment: Chloroquine plus primaquine for radical cure (check G6PD first)

bugs.name: Pneumocystis jirovecii
bugs.symptoms: Subacute dry cough and dyspnea; ground-glass opacities; occurs at CD4 < 200

bugs.name: Pseudomonas aeruginosa
bugs.symptoms: Necrotic ulcer with black eschar in neutropenia; blue-green pigment

bugs.name: Rickettsia prowazekii
bugs.geography: Crowding/war zones; Central and South America
bugs.symptoms: Fever, headache, centrifugal rash sparing palms/soles; Brill-Zinsser recrudescence

bugs.name: Rickettsia rickettsii
bugs.geography: Southeastern US (NC, TN, AR, MO, VA)
bugs.symptoms: Fever, headache; rash starting on wrists/ankles spreading centripetally

bugs.name: Rubella virus
bugs.symptoms: Mild fine maculopapular rash; posterior auricular lymphadenopathy

bugs.name: SARS-CoV-2
bugs.symptoms: Respiratory illness; cytokine storm causing ARDS and septic shock; binds ACE2 receptor
bugs.treatment: Dexamethasone in late inflammatory phase (harmful if given early)

bugs.name: Staphylococcus aureus
bugs.symptoms: Furuncle/carbuncle; pus-producing wound; coagulase-positive

bugs.name: Staphylococcus epidermidis
bugs.symptoms: Indolent device infection; biofilm-forming, coagulase-negative

bugs.name: Staphylococcus saprophyticus
bugs.symptoms: Dysuria, frequency; coagulase-negative, novobiocin-resistant

bugs.name: Streptococcus pyogenes
bugs.symptoms: Bright raised erysipelas; pharyngitis; pain out of proportion in nec fasc
bugs.treatment: Penicillin; surgical debridement for necrotizing fasciitis

bugs.name: Toxoplasma gondii
bugs.symptoms: Fever, headache, confusion, motor deficits, or seizures; space-occupying gray matter lesion on CT/MRI

bugs.name: Trichomonas vaginalis
bugs.symptoms: Frothy green-yellow discharge; strawberry cervix; motile trophozoite

bugs.name: Trichophyton rubrum
bugs.symptoms: Annular scaly plaque with central clearing; branching hyphae on KOH
bugs.treatment: Topical antifungals; oral terbinafine for widespread disease

bugs.name: Trypanosoma brucei gambiense
bugs.symptoms: Chronic course; Winterbottom's sign; somnolence progressing to coma
bugs.treatment: Fexinidazole (oral); NECT for severe CNS disease

bugs.name: Trypanosoma brucei rhodesiense
bugs.symptoms: Acute, rapidly fatal; fever, lymphadenopathy, CNS decline
bugs.treatment: Fexinidazole early; melarsoprol + prednisolone for late CNS

bugs.name: Trypanosoma cruzi
bugs.geography: Rural areas from southern Texas (U.S.) through Central and South America
bugs.symptoms: Romana's sign (swollen eye); chronic megacolon, megaesophagus, dilated cardiomyopathy

bugs.name: Varicella-zoster virus
bugs.symptoms: Dewdrop-on-rose-petal vesicles in varying stages; dermatomal rash in zoster

bugs.name: Yellow Fever virus
bugs.symptoms: Triad of high fever, jaundice, and black vomit; Councilman bodies on liver biopsy
bugs.treatment: Supportive care; live-attenuated vaccine for prevention

bugs.name: Yersinia enterocolitica
bugs.symptoms: RLQ pain mimicking appendicitis with bloody diarrhea in a child
bugs.treatment: Often self-limited; severe cases doxycycline or TMP-SMX

bugs.name: Yersinia pestis
bugs.symptoms: Painful inguinal buboes; flea bite; digital gangrene

bugs.name: Zika virus
bugs.symptoms: Mild rash and conjunctivitis in adults; severe fetal microcephaly if infected in pregnancy

drugs.name: 5-Fluorouracil
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits thymidylate synthase causing thymine-less death

drugs.name: 6-Mercaptopurine
drugs.mechanism: Converted via HGPRT to toxic thioguanine nucleotides that inhibit de novo purine synthesis and incorporate into DNA causing strand breaks
drugs.adverseEffects: Toxic accumulation with allopurinol; reduce dose 75%

drugs.name: Abacavir (ABC)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (NRTI backbone partner with lamivudine)
drugs.mechanism: Guanosine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA
drugs.adverseEffects: Fatal hypersensitivity in HLA-B*5701 carriers; never rechallenge

drugs.name: Alteplase (tPA)
drugs.mechanism: Converts plasminogen to plasmin, which digests the fibrin mesh of a clot
drugs.adverseEffects: Intracranial hemorrhage; contraindicated with prior ICH

drugs.name: Amphotericin B
drugs.mechanism: Binds ergosterol forming membrane pores in fungal cells

drugs.name: Argatroban
drugs.mechanism: Direct thrombin inhibitor

drugs.name: Artemisinins (Artemether, Artesunate)
drugs.mechanism: Binds free heme iron in food vacuole forming covalent complexes; disrupts heme detoxification and increases oxidative stress - structural damage, inhibition of nucleic acid and protein synthesis; endoperoxide bridge essential for activity
drugs.adverseEffects: Generally well tolerated; black-water fever at high parasite burden

drugs.name: Aspirin
drugs.disease: Antiplatelet prophylaxis for MI and stroke
drugs.mechanism: Irreversibly acetylates COX-1, abolishing thromboxane A2 synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: GI ulcers; tinnitus and mixed acid-base disturbance at high doses

drugs.name: Atazanavir
drugs.mechanism: Protease inhibitor blocking gag/gag-pol polyprotein cleavage

drugs.name: Atovaquone-Proguanil
drugs.mechanism: Atovaquone collapses parasite mitochondrial bc1; proguanil inhibits DHFR
drugs.adverseEffects: Generally well tolerated; GI upset, headache, transaminitis

drugs.name: ATRA (all-trans retinoic acid)
drugs.mechanism: Forces malignant promyelocytes to differentiate and mature

drugs.name: Benznidazole
drugs.mechanism: Nitroreductase-activated free radical generator
drugs.adverseEffects: Photosensitive dermatitis; peripheral neuropathy; marrow suppression

drugs.name: Benzodiazepines (lorazepam/diazepam)
drugs.disease: Shivering suppression during heat stroke cooling
drugs.mechanism: GABA-A potentiation suppressing the shivering reflex

drugs.name: Bevacizumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody that binds and neutralizes VEGF

drugs.name: Bictegravir (BIC)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (first-line third agent, fixed-dose Biktarvy)
drugs.mechanism: Second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)
drugs.adverseEffects: Weight gain; well tolerated, high resistance barrier

drugs.name: Bleomycin
drugs.mechanism: Generates free radicals causing DNA strand breaks

drugs.name: Bortezomib
drugs.mechanism: Proteasome inhibitor blocking NF-kB; misfolded proteins accumulate

drugs.name: Cabotegravir (CAB)
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting injectable integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)
drugs.adverseEffects: Injection-site reactions; gluteal IM every 4-8 weeks

drugs.name: CAR T-cell therapy
drugs.disease: Relapsed CD19-positive B-cell malignancies (ALL, DLBCL, FL, MCL); BCMA-positive multiple myeloma
drugs.mechanism: Patient T cells engineered to express artificial receptors targeting specific tumor antigens (CD19 or BCMA); antigen-binding and T-cell-activating functions combined in one receptor
drugs.adverseEffects: Cytokine release syndrome (high fever, multi-organ failure)

drugs.name: Carboplatin
drugs.mechanism: DNA cross-linking, less reactive than cisplatin

drugs.name: Cetuximab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against EGFR
drugs.adverseEffects: Ineffective if KRAS is mutated; acneiform rash

drugs.name: Checkpoint inhibitors (anti-PD-1, anti-CTLA-4)
drugs.mechanism: Block T-cell checkpoints to unleash anti-tumor immune response

drugs.name: Chloroquine / Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.mechanism: Blocks heme polymerization into hemozoin, so toxic free heme damages parasite
drugs.adverseEffects: Retinopathy and cardiotoxicity with chronic high-dose use

drugs.name: Cisplatin
drugs.mechanism: Aquated intermediate cross-links DNA

drugs.name: Clindamycin
drugs.disease: Toxic shock syndrome and necrotizing soft-tissue infection
drugs.mechanism: Ribosomal inhibitor that suppresses bacterial exotoxin production

drugs.name: Clopidogrel
drugs.disease: Antiplatelet therapy for ACS and post-stent
drugs.mechanism: Irreversible P2Y12 ADP-receptor blocker; prodrug activated by CYP2C19
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding; ineffective in CYP2C19 poor metabolizers; rare neutropenia

drugs.name: Cyclophosphamide
drugs.mechanism: Pro-drug; alkylates DNA at N7 of guanine causing cross-links
drugs.adverseEffects: Hemorrhagic cystitis from acrolein; prevented with MESNA

drugs.name: Cytarabine (Ara-C)
drugs.mechanism: Arabinose analog blocks DNA polymerase and terminates chains

drugs.name: Dabigatran
drugs.disease: AFib stroke prevention and DVT/PE treatment
drugs.mechanism: Direct oral inhibitor binding the active site of thrombin (IIa)

drugs.name: Dapsone
drugs.mechanism: Sulfone with anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial activity
drugs.adverseEffects: Hemolysis, especially in G6PD deficiency; methemoglobinemia

drugs.name: Darunavir
drugs.mechanism: Protease inhibitor blocking gag/gag-pol polyprotein cleavage
drugs.adverseEffects: Sulfa-moiety rash; avoid in sulfa allergy; hepatotoxicity

drugs.name: Dobutamine
drugs.mechanism: Beta-agonist augmenting cardiac contractility without vasoconstriction

drugs.name: Dolutegravir (DTG)
drugs.mechanism: Second-generation integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)
drugs.adverseEffects: Weight gain; high resistance barrier and well tolerated

drugs.name: Doxorubicin (Red Devil)
drugs.mechanism: Generates free radicals and intercalates DNA

drugs.name: Doxycycline
drugs.disease: Lyme disease, RMSF, ehrlichiosis, anaplasmosis, Q fever
drugs.mechanism: Tetracycline inhibiting bacterial 30S ribosomal protein synthesis

drugs.name: Echinocandins (caspofungin)
drugs.mechanism: Inhibit beta-1,3-glucan synthase, cracking the fungal cell wall
drugs.adverseEffects: GI upset (diarrhea, nausea); flushing/urticaria (histamine-mediated); elevated LFTs/hepatitis; phlebitis at infusion site

drugs.name: Eculizumab
drugs.mechanism: Anti-C5 monoclonal antibody blocking terminal complement
drugs.adverseEffects: Increased risk of Neisseria meningitidis infection

drugs.name: Efavirenz
drugs.mechanism: Non-nucleoside allosteric reverse transcriptase inhibitor

drugs.name: Eflornithine
drugs.disease: Severe late-stage Gambiense HAT (part of NECT)
drugs.mechanism: Suicide inhibitor of ornithine decarboxylase, blocking polyamine synthesis

drugs.name: Emtricitabine (FTC)
drugs.mechanism: Cytidine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA

drugs.name: Enfuvirtide
drugs.mechanism: gp41 fusion inhibitor; 36-amino-acid synthetic peptide

drugs.name: Epoetin alfa (ESA)
drugs.disease: Anemia of chronic kidney disease or chemotherapy
drugs.mechanism: Binds EPO receptor on erythroid progenitors, activating JAK-STAT
drugs.adverseEffects: Hypertension; thrombosis/stroke/MI/VTE (black box); pure red cell aplasia (CKD, subQ); shortened survival in cancer patients

drugs.name: Etoposide
drugs.mechanism: Blocks topoisomerase II resealing of double-strand DNA breaks

drugs.name: Ferrous sulfate (oral iron)
drugs.mechanism: Replaces depleted iron stores; absorbed as Fe2+ in the duodenum

drugs.name: Fexinidazole
drugs.disease: Early- and late-stage African trypanosomiasis (sleeping sickness)
drugs.mechanism: Nitroimidazole activated by nitroreductase; oral, crosses the BBB
drugs.adverseEffects: Neuropsychiatric effects (agitation, anxiety, hallucination, psychosis); neutropenia; QTc prolongation

drugs.name: Fluconazole
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits fungal 14-alpha-demethylase; best CNS penetration; no mold activity
drugs.adverseEffects: Hepatotoxicity; QT prolongation; CYP drug interactions

drugs.name: Flucytosine
drugs.mechanism: Converted by fungal cytosine deaminase to 5-FU, blocking DNA/RNA synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: Bone marrow suppression from gut conversion to 5-FU

drugs.name: Folic acid (folate)
drugs.mechanism: Restores tetrahydrofolate for DNA synthesis
drugs.adverseEffects: Masks vitamin B12 deficiency: corrects anemia while neurological damage progresses unnoticed (worsening may be irreversible)

drugs.name: Fondaparinux
drugs.disease: Anticoagulation, preferred if history of HIT
drugs.mechanism: Synthetic pentasaccharide that exclusively inhibits factor Xa via antithrombin

drugs.name: Griseofulvin
drugs.mechanism: Binds fungal microtubules disrupting mitosis; deposits in keratin
drugs.adverseEffects: CYP450 induction; disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol

drugs.name: Hydroxocobalamin (Cyanokit)
drugs.disease: Cyanide poisoning (also a form of B12)
drugs.mechanism: Binds cyanide to form non-toxic cyanocobalamin
drugs.adverseEffects: Reddish discoloration of skin and urine

drugs.name: Hydroxychloroquine
drugs.mechanism: Antimalarial immunomodulator reducing autoimmune inflammation

drugs.name: Hydroxyurea
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, inducing fetal hemoglobin (HbF)

drugs.name: Icatibant
drugs.mechanism: Bradykinin B2 receptor antagonist
drugs.adverseEffects: Injection-site reactions; ineffective for histaminergic angioedema

drugs.name: Imatinib
drugs.mechanism: Tyrosine kinase inhibitor blocking BCR-ABL ATP-binding site
drugs.adverseEffects: Periorbital edema; T315I mutation confers resistance

drugs.name: Intramuscular epinephrine
drugs.disease: Anaphylaxis with urticaria and airway compromise
drugs.mechanism: Alpha/beta agonist reversing vasodilation and bronchospasm

drugs.name: Ipilimumab
drugs.mechanism: CTLA-4 inhibitor that enhances T-cell activation

drugs.name: Irinotecan
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug converted to active SN-38 by carboxylesterase; SN-38 forms drug-topoisomerase I-DNA ternary complex preventing DNA strand resealing

drugs.name: Iron dextran / iron sucrose (IV iron)
drugs.disease: Iron deficiency anemia with malabsorption or rapid blood loss
drugs.mechanism: Parenteral iron repletion bypassing the closed gut
drugs.adverseEffects: Iron dextran (low-MW): anaphylaxis risk, test dose required; other IV iron products (iron sucrose, etc.): no test dose required; all: infusion reactions (flushing, headache, hypotension)

drugs.name: Isotretinoin
drugs.mechanism: Oral retinoid normalizing keratinization and reducing sebum

drugs.name: Itraconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole inhibiting 14-alpha-demethylase; needs acidic gastric pH
drugs.adverseEffects: Negative inotrope; avoid in heart failure

drugs.name: Ketoconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole inhibiting 14-alpha-demethylase

drugs.name: Lamivudine (3TC)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (NRTI backbone); also hepatitis B
drugs.mechanism: Cytidine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA

drugs.name: Lenacapavir
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection in heavily treatment-experienced patients
drugs.mechanism: Capsid inhibitor disrupting uncoating, nuclear import, assembly

drugs.name: Lenalidomide
drugs.mechanism: Binds cereblon, degrading transcription factors cancer cells need

drugs.name: Leucovorin (folinic acid)
drugs.mechanism: Reduced folate that bypasses blocked DHFR to rescue normal cells

drugs.name: Low Molecular Weight Heparin (Enoxaparin)
drugs.disease: DVT/PE treatment and prophylaxis; anticoagulation in pregnancy
drugs.mechanism: Antithrombin-mediated inhibition predominantly of factor Xa
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding; lower HIT risk; accumulates in renal failure

drugs.name: Maraviroc
drugs.mechanism: Entry inhibitor that binds the CCR5 co-receptor blocking viral attachment
drugs.adverseEffects: Requires coreceptor tropism assay before use; ineffective if CXCR4-tropic virus present

drugs.name: Mefloquine
drugs.disease: Prophylaxis and treatment of chloroquine-resistant malaria
drugs.mechanism: Blood schizonticide of unclear mechanism
drugs.adverseEffects: Neuropsychiatric: anxiety, depression, confusion (prodrome to paranoia, hallucinations, psychosis); dizziness/vertigo, loss of balance; contraindicated in major psychiatric disorders

drugs.name: Melarsoprol
drugs.disease: Late-stage Rhodesiense HAT with CNS involvement
drugs.mechanism: Trivalent arsenical binding parasite trypanothione and enzymes

drugs.name: MESNA
drugs.mechanism: Thiol that concentrates in bladder and neutralizes acrolein

drugs.name: Methotrexate
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, blocking active folate

drugs.name: Metronidazole
drugs.mechanism: Prodrug activated by parasite nitroreductase to DNA-damaging radicals
drugs.adverseEffects: Metallic taste; nausea; headache; disulfiram-like reaction with alcohol not supported by current evidence

drugs.name: Miltefosine
drugs.mechanism: Disrupts parasite phospholipid metabolism; only oral antileishmanial

drugs.name: Nevirapine
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection; presumptive therapy in high-risk neonates
drugs.mechanism: Non-nucleoside allosteric reverse transcriptase inhibitor

drugs.name: Nifedipine
drugs.mechanism: Calcium channel blocker causing peripheral vasodilation

drugs.name: Nystatin
drugs.mechanism: Polyene binding ergosterol; topical/oral non-absorbed only
drugs.adverseEffects: Too toxic for systemic use; minimal with topical use

drugs.name: Oxaliplatin
drugs.mechanism: DNA cross-linking via aquated platinum intermediate
drugs.adverseEffects: Peripheral neuropathy acute (exacerbated by cold) and delayed progressive neuropathy

drugs.name: Paclitaxel (taxane)
drugs.mechanism: Hyperstabilizes microtubules, blocking disassembly

drugs.name: Paromomycin
drugs.disease: Luminal eradication of intestinal amebic cysts
drugs.mechanism: Aminoglycoside binding 16S rRNA on 30S ribosome; not orally absorbed
drugs.adverseEffects: GI upset only (oral); aminoglycoside toxicity if parenteral

drugs.name: Pembrolizumab
drugs.disease: Metastatic melanoma and other cancers (checkpoint inhibitor)
drugs.mechanism: PD-1 inhibitor that releases the brakes on T cells

drugs.name: Pentamidine
drugs.disease: Early-stage Gambiense HAT in young children
drugs.mechanism: Binds parasite kinetoplast DNA; IV/IM only, poor CNS penetration

drugs.name: Pentavalent antimonials
drugs.mechanism: Reduced to trivalent antimony, binding parasite sulfhydryl groups
drugs.adverseEffects: Cumulative cardiac, pancreatic, renal, and marrow toxicity

drugs.name: Posaconazole
drugs.disease: Mucormycosis and prophylaxis in prolonged neutropenia
drugs.mechanism: Azole with extended spectrum covering Mucorales

drugs.name: Primaquine
drugs.disease: Radical cure of P. vivax/ovale (hypnozoite eradication)
drugs.mechanism: 8-aminoquinoline; mechanism of action unknown (slide p.48, p.61)
drugs.adverseEffects: Acute hemolytic anemia in G6PD deficiency; screen G6PD first

drugs.name: Pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin
drugs.mechanism: Sequential folate synthesis inhibition (DHFR + DHPS); leucovorin rescue
drugs.adverseEffects: Bone marrow suppression mitigated by leucovorin

drugs.name: Quinine
drugs.mechanism: Blood schizonticide of poorly understood mechanism

drugs.name: Raltegravir (RAL)
drugs.mechanism: First-generation INSTI metabolized by UGT1A1, not CYP
drugs.adverseEffects: Lower resistance barrier; no CYP-based drug interactions

drugs.name: RhoGAM (anti-D immunoglobulin)
drugs.disease: Prevention of Rh hemolytic disease of the newborn
drugs.mechanism: Passive anti-D IgG clears fetal RBCs before maternal sensitization
drugs.adverseEffects: Well tolerated; given at 28 weeks and within 72h of delivery

drugs.name: Rilpivirine
drugs.mechanism: Non-nucleoside allosteric reverse transcriptase inhibitor
drugs.adverseEffects: Needs acid stomach for absorption; virologic failure at high VL

drugs.name: Ritonavir / Cobicistat
drugs.disease: Pharmacokinetic boosting of HIV protease inhibitors
drugs.mechanism: Potent CYP3A4 inhibitor that raises partner PI levels

drugs.name: Rituximab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody targeting CD20 on B cells

drugs.name: Rivaroxaban / Apixaban
drugs.disease: AFib stroke prevention and DVT/PE treatment
drugs.mechanism: Direct oral inhibitors of factor Xa
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding (no specific antidote; PCC for reversal - andexanet alfa withdrawn from US market)

drugs.name: Spiramycin
drugs.disease: First-trimester toxoplasmosis to prevent vertical transmission
drugs.mechanism: Macrolide that concentrates in the placenta
drugs.adverseEffects: Minimal fetal exposure; does not treat established fetal infection

drugs.name: Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine
drugs.disease: Intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy (IPTp)
drugs.mechanism: Synergistic folate inhibition (blocks dihydropteroate synthase and DHFR)

drugs.name: Suramin
drugs.disease: Early-stage Rhodesiense HAT in young children
drugs.mechanism: Polyanion inhibiting parasite glycolytic enzymes and NADH oxidation

drugs.name: Tafenoquine
drugs.disease: Radical cure and prophylaxis of malaria
drugs.mechanism: Long-acting 8-aminoquinoline; mechanism of action unknown (slide p.48, p.61)

drugs.name: Tenofovir (TDF/TAF)
drugs.disease: HIV-1 infection (NRTI backbone); also hepatitis B
drugs.mechanism: Nucleotide reverse transcriptase inhibitor causing DNA chain termination
drugs.adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity (Fanconi syndrome) and decreased bone density; TAF milder

drugs.name: Terbinafine
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits squalene epoxidase; ergosterol depletion plus toxic squalene buildup

drugs.name: Ticagrelor
drugs.mechanism: Reversible P2Y12 inhibitor not requiring hepatic activation
drugs.adverseEffects: Dyspnea unrelated to heart failure; bleeding

drugs.name: TMP-SMX
drugs.disease: Treatment and prophylaxis of Pneumocystis pneumonia
drugs.mechanism: Sequential folate-synthesis inhibition

drugs.name: Topical 5-fluorouracil
drugs.disease: Actinic keratosis and superficial basal cell carcinoma
drugs.mechanism: Pyrimidine analog inhibiting thymidylate synthase in atypical cells
drugs.adverseEffects: Local erythema, erosion, and inflammation at treated sites

drugs.name: Trastuzumab
drugs.mechanism: Monoclonal antibody against the HER2/neu receptor

drugs.name: Unfractionated Heparin
drugs.mechanism: Binds antithrombin III, accelerating inactivation of thrombin (IIa) and factor Xa

drugs.name: Vemurafenib
drugs.mechanism: BRAF kinase inhibitor blocking RAS/MAPK proliferation signaling
drugs.adverseEffects: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinomas; combine with MEK inhibitor

drugs.name: Vincristine
drugs.mechanism: Blocks microtubule assembly, arresting mitosis
drugs.adverseEffects: Peripheral neuropathy, constipation; fatal if given intrathecally

drugs.name: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin)
drugs.mechanism: Cofactor for methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA conversion
drugs.adverseEffects: Well tolerated; must rule out before giving folate alone

drugs.name: Voriconazole
drugs.mechanism: Azole blocking ergosterol synthesis via 14-alpha-demethylase
drugs.adverseEffects: Visual disturbances / photopsia; phototoxicity raising SCC risk

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits VKORC1, blocking gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C/S
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding, skin necrosis, teratogenic (reverse with vitamin K or PCC/FFP)

drugs.name: Zidovudine (AZT)
drugs.disease: HIV vertical-transmission prevention in pregnancy and neonates
drugs.mechanism: Thymidine-analog NRTI; chain termination of proviral DNA

drugs.name: Capecitabine
drugs.disease: Colorectal and other solid tumors (oral 5-FU prodrug)
drugs.mechanism: Oral prodrug converted in liver and tumor to 5-FU, which inhibits thymidylate synthase

drugs.name: Gemcitabine
drugs.disease: Pancreatic, non-small cell lung, ovarian, and bladder cancers
drugs.mechanism: Difluoro-deoxycytidine analog; triphosphate inhibits DNA polymerase and causes chain termination
drugs.adverseEffects: Myelosuppression, flu-like symptoms, hepatic enzyme elevations

drugs.name: Daunorubicin
drugs.mechanism: Anthracycline; intercalates DNA, inhibits topoisomerase II, and generates free radicals

drugs.name: Idarubicin
drugs.mechanism: Anthracycline; intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II

drugs.name: Mitoxantrone
drugs.disease: Acute myeloid leukemia, prostate cancer, multiple sclerosis
drugs.mechanism: Anthracenedione; intercalates DNA and inhibits topoisomerase II
drugs.adverseEffects: Cardiotoxicity, blue-green discoloration of urine and sclerae

drugs.name: Mitomycin
drugs.disease: Bladder, anal, and upper GI cancers
drugs.mechanism: Bioreductive alkylator that crosslinks DNA after cellular activation

drugs.name: Dactinomycin
drugs.mechanism: Intercalates DNA and blocks DNA-dependent RNA polymerase

drugs.name: Topotecan
drugs.mechanism: Camptothecin; inhibits topoisomerase I, stabilizing the cleavage complex

drugs.name: Docetaxel
drugs.disease: Breast, prostate, and non-small cell lung cancers
drugs.mechanism: Taxane; stabilizes microtubules and arrests cells in M phase
drugs.adverseEffects: Neutropenia, fluid retention, peripheral neuropathy, hypersensitivity

drugs.name: Teniposide
drugs.mechanism: Podophyllotoxin; inhibits topoisomerase II

drugs.name: Nivolumab
drugs.disease: Melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, renal cell carcinoma
drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-1 monoclonal antibody; releases T-cell inhibition of tumor
drugs.adverseEffects: Immune-related adverse events (colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies)

drugs.name: Atezolizumab
drugs.disease: Urothelial carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, triple-negative breast cancer
drugs.mechanism: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody; blocks tumor PD-L1 engagement of T-cell PD-1
drugs.adverseEffects: Immune-related adverse events (colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathies)

drugs.name: Tisagenlecleucel
drugs.disease: B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia (pediatric/young adult), refractory DLBCL
drugs.mechanism: Anti-CD19 chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy; autologous engineered T cells
drugs.adverseEffects: Cytokine release syndrome, neurotoxicity (ICANS), B-cell aplasia

drugs.name: Desmopressin (DDAVP)
drugs.disease: Mild hemophilia A, von Willebrand disease, central diabetes insipidus
drugs.mechanism: Vasopressin V2 receptor agonist; releases vWF and factor VIII from endothelial stores

drugs.name: Emicizumab
drugs.disease: Hemophilia A (including patients with factor VIII inhibitors)
drugs.mechanism: Bispecific monoclonal antibody that bridges activated factor IX and factor X, mimicking factor VIIIa
drugs.adverseEffects: Thrombotic microangiopathy when given with activated prothrombin complex

drugs.name: Aminocaproic acid
drugs.disease: Hyperfibrinolysis (e.g., post-cardiac-surgery bleeding, DIC with fibrinolysis)
drugs.mechanism: Lysine analog; blocks plasminogen activation and binding to fibrin
drugs.adverseEffects: Thrombosis, hypotension, myopathy with prolonged use

drugs.name: Bivalirudin
drugs.disease: Anticoagulation during PCI and cardiac surgery; HIT
drugs.mechanism: Direct thrombin inhibitor; bivalent reversible hirudin analog
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding (shorter half-life than other DTIs makes it more controllable)

drugs.name: Edoxaban
drugs.disease: Atrial fibrillation, VTE treatment and prevention
drugs.mechanism: Direct oral factor Xa inhibitor (DOAC)
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding; reduced efficacy at high CrCl

drugs.name: Cilostazol
drugs.disease: Intermittent claudication in peripheral arterial disease
drugs.mechanism: Phosphodiesterase-3 inhibitor; increases platelet cAMP and causes vasodilation
drugs.adverseEffects: Headache, palpitations; contraindicated in heart failure

drugs.name: Dipyridamole
drugs.disease: Secondary stroke prevention (with aspirin); pharmacologic stress testing
drugs.mechanism: Inhibits adenosine reuptake and phosphodiesterase, raising cAMP and producing antiplatelet and vasodilatory effects

drugs.name: Lepirudin
drugs.mechanism: Direct thrombin inhibitor; recombinant hirudin from leech salivary gland

drugs.name: Desirudin
drugs.disease: DVT prophylaxis following hip replacement surgery
drugs.mechanism: Direct thrombin inhibitor; hirudin analog given subcutaneously

drugs.name: Betrixaban
drugs.disease: Extended VTE prophylaxis in acutely ill hospitalized medical patients
drugs.mechanism: Direct oral factor Xa inhibitor (DOAC)

drugs.name: Tenecteplase
drugs.mechanism: Recombinant tPA variant with longer half-life and greater fibrin specificity; single IV bolus

drugs.name: Reteplase
drugs.disease: ST-elevation myocardial infarction, massive pulmonary embolism
drugs.mechanism: Recombinant tPA deletion mutant; activates plasminogen to plasmin

drugs.name: Streptokinase
drugs.disease: Acute MI (historical, largely replaced by tPA variants)
drugs.mechanism: Bacterial protein from beta-hemolytic streptococci; forms complex with plasminogen, producing a systemic lytic state
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding, allergic reaction/hypersensitivity (antigenic); cannot re-administer within 6 months

drugs.name: Urokinase
drugs.disease: Massive pulmonary embolism, occluded catheter clearance
drugs.mechanism: Human renal enzyme; direct plasminogen activator

drugs.name: Prasugrel
drugs.disease: Acute coronary syndrome managed with PCI (dual antiplatelet therapy)
drugs.mechanism: P2Y12 ADP receptor inhibitor; irreversible thienopyridine prodrug with more efficient activation than clopidogrel
drugs.adverseEffects: Bleeding (greater than clopidogrel); contraindicated in prior stroke/TIA

drugs.name: Cangrelor
drugs.disease: PCI adjunct when oral P2Y12 loading is not feasible
drugs.mechanism: P2Y12 ADP receptor inhibitor; reversible IV ADP analog with rapid onset and offset

drugs.name: Abciximab
drugs.disease: PCI and non-ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome
drugs.mechanism: GP IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitor; Fab fragment of a monoclonal antibody

drugs.name: Eptifibatide
drugs.mechanism: GP IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitor; cyclic heptapeptide

drugs.name: Tirofiban
drugs.mechanism: GP IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitor; small-molecule non-peptide

drugs.name: Ticlopidine
drugs.disease: Stroke prevention (largely replaced by safer P2Y12 inhibitors)
drugs.mechanism: P2Y12 ADP receptor inhibitor; irreversible thienopyridine

drugs.name: Ribavirin
drugs.disease: Lassa fever and other arenavirus/bunyavirus hemorrhagic fevers
drugs.mechanism: Guanosine analog; multiple antiviral mechanisms including inosine monophosphate dehydrogenase inhibition

drugs.name: Ganciclovir
drugs.disease: CMV retinitis, esophagitis, and disseminated disease in immunocompromised
drugs.mechanism: Acyclic guanosine analog phosphorylated by viral UL97 kinase; inhibits CMV DNA polymerase

drugs.name: Valganciclovir
drugs.disease: CMV treatment and prophylaxis in transplant recipients (oral)
drugs.mechanism: Oral prodrug rapidly hydrolyzed to ganciclovir; inhibits CMV DNA polymerase

drugs.name: Cidofovir
drugs.mechanism: Cytidine nucleotide analog; inhibits viral DNA polymerase without requiring viral kinase activation
drugs.adverseEffects: Severe nephrotoxicity (give with IV saline and probenecid)

drugs.name: Foscarnet
drugs.mechanism: Pyrophosphate analog; directly inhibits viral DNA and reverse transcriptase polymerases without activation
drugs.adverseEffects: Nephrotoxicity, electrolyte disturbances (hypocalcemia, hypomagnesemia, hypokalemia), seizures

drugs.name: Imiquimod
drugs.disease: Actinic keratosis, superficial basal cell carcinoma, external genital warts
drugs.mechanism: Topical TLR7 agonist; induces local cytokine release and cell-mediated immune response

drugs.name: Didanosine (ddI)
drugs.disease: HIV (first-generation NRTI, no longer marketed in US)
drugs.mechanism: Adenosine analog NRTI; inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and causes chain termination
drugs.adverseEffects: Pancreatitis, peripheral neuropathy, lactic acidosis with hepatic steatosis

drugs.name: Stavudine (d4T)
drugs.disease: HIV (first-generation thymidine NRTI, no longer marketed in US)
drugs.mechanism: Thymidine analog NRTI; inhibits HIV reverse transcriptase and causes chain termination
drugs.adverseEffects: Lipoatrophy, peripheral neuropathy, lactic acidosis with hepatic steatosis

drugs.name: Lopinavir
drugs.disease: HIV (older protease inhibitor, always co-formulated with ritonavir boost)
drugs.mechanism: HIV protease inhibitor; prevents cleavage of viral polyprotein
drugs.adverseEffects: GI intolerance, dyslipidemia, insulin resistance; high pill burden

drugs.name: Fosamprenavir
drugs.disease: HIV (protease inhibitor, prodrug of amprenavir; not preferred for initial therapy)
drugs.mechanism: HIV protease inhibitor; prevents cleavage of viral polyprotein

correlates.name: Abacavir Hypersensitivity Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Abacavir binds HLA-B*5701, creating a neo-self-antigen recognized by cytotoxic T cells
correlates.treatment: Stop abacavir permanently; never rechallenge (can be fatal)
correlates.presentation: 32M with HIV started on abacavir 9 days ago presents with fever, rash, GI symptoms, and dyspnea; HLA-B*5701 positive

correlates.name: Acanthosis Nigricans
correlates.pathophysiology: Insulin/IGF-1 stimulation of keratinocytes; or paraneoplastic with GI adenocarcinoma
correlates.treatment: Treat insulin resistance; investigate GI cancer if sudden in older adults
correlates.presentation: 45F with obesity and type 2 diabetes has velvety hyperpigmented plaques in the axillae and posterior neck

correlates.name: Accidental Hypothermia
correlates.pathophysiology: Core temperature below 35 C impairs metabolism, causing bradyarrhythmias and arrest
correlates.treatment: Staged rewarming (passive to active core/ECMO); not dead until warm and dead
correlates.presentation: 60M alcoholic found outdoors overnight; core temperature 28°C, J waves on ECG, altered mental status

correlates.name: Acne Vulgaris
correlates.pathophysiology: Follicular hyperkeratinization, androgenic sebum overproduction, C. acnes, and inflammation
correlates.treatment: Topical retinoids and benzoyl peroxide; antibiotics; isotretinoin for severe disease
correlates.presentation: 16F with comedones, inflammatory papules, and pustules on the face, chest, and back

correlates.name: Acral Lentiginous Melanoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Subtype of melanoma arising on palms, soles, nail beds, and mucous membranes; not UV-related
correlates.treatment: Wide local excision with sentinel node biopsy; advanced disease: immunotherapy
correlates.presentation: 63F notices a dark longitudinal streak under her toenail extending onto the proximal nail fold (Hutchinson sign); most common melanoma in African-Americans, Latinos, and Asians

correlates.name: Acrochordons (Skin Tags)
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign outgrowths of normal skin at sites of friction; associated with obesity, diabetes, and colonic polyps
correlates.treatment: Scissor excision or electrodessication for cosmesis or irritation
correlates.presentation: 64F with obesity has soft, flesh-colored pedunculated papules on her posterior neck, axillae, and under her breasts that become irritated by jewelry

correlates.name: Acrodermatitis Enteropathica
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal recessive defect in intestinal zinc absorption causing zinc deficiency in infants
correlates.treatment: Oral zinc sulfate supplementation
correlates.presentation: Infant with vesiculobullous erythematous dermatitis in acral, perioral, and perirectal distribution, alopecia, diarrhea, and growth retardation; responds rapidly to zinc

correlates.name: Actinic Keratosis
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced p53 mutation causing partial-thickness keratinocyte atypia; precursor to SCC
correlates.treatment: Cryotherapy, topical 5-FU, imiquimod, photodynamic therapy
correlates.presentation: 70M farmer with rough scaly erythematous papules on sun-exposed scalp and forearms

correlates.name: Acute Chest Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Multi-factorial (infection, fat embolism, infarction) causing new pulmonary infiltrate and respiratory symptoms; leading cause of death in SCD
correlates.treatment: Oxygen; antibiotics; exchange transfusion if severe
correlates.presentation: 12-year-old with sickle cell disease has fever, chest pain, hypoxia, and a new pulmonary infiltrate

correlates.name: Acute Graft-versus-Host Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Donor immunocompetent T cells from a bone marrow transplant attack histo-incompatible host tissues in skin, liver, and gut
correlates.treatment: High-dose corticosteroids; calcineurin inhibitors; severe cases need ICU care like TEN
correlates.presentation: Patient 14-100 days post-BMT has classic maculopapular rash, hyperbilirubinemia, and profuse diarrhea; severe cases progress to TEN-like bullous sloughing

correlates.name: Acute hemolytic transfusion reaction (AHTR)
correlates.pathophysiology: ABO incompatibility (clerical error); preformed IgM fixes complement causing intravascular hemolysis
correlates.treatment: Stop transfusion; IV fluids, pressors, diuresis for renal protection
correlates.presentation: 45F develops fever, back pain, dark urine, and hypotension during transfusion of ABO-incompatible blood

correlates.name: Acute leukemia (marrow crowding)
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant blast expansion fills marrow, crowding out normal lineages causing pancytopenia
correlates.treatment: Induction chemotherapy; lineage-directed therapy after flow cytometry
correlates.presentation: 7-year-old with weeks of fatigue, easy bruising, fever, and pallor; pancytopenia on CBC

correlates.name: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL)
correlates.pathophysiology: Clonal proliferation of TdT-positive lymphoblasts; most common childhood cancer
correlates.treatment: Multi-agent chemotherapy with CNS prophylaxis
correlates.presentation: 5-year-old with bone pain, fevers, lymphadenopathy, and pancytopenia; >20% TdT+ lymphoblasts on marrow biopsy

correlates.name: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML)
correlates.pathophysiology: Clonal expansion of myeloid blasts; Auer rods of crystallized myeloperoxidase
correlates.treatment: Induction chemotherapy (e.g., cytarabine-based)
correlates.presentation: 55M with fatigue and gum bleeding; circulating myeloblasts with Auer rods on peripheral smear

correlates.name: Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL/M3)
correlates.pathophysiology: t(15;17) disrupts the retinoic acid receptor; granule release triggers DIC
correlates.treatment: ATRA (all-trans retinoic acid) to force differentiation
correlates.presentation: 35F with bleeding from multiple sites; promyelocytes with bundles of Auer rods, t(15;17), and DIC

correlates.name: Acute Retroviral Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Initial high-level HIV viremia 2-4 weeks after exposure causes a mononucleosis-like illness
correlates.treatment: Initiate antiretroviral therapy
correlates.presentation: 25M with recent high-risk sexual exposure has a mono-like illness; HIV RNA positive, ELISA negative

correlates.name: AIDS
correlates.pathophysiology: Progressive HIV depletion of CD4 T-cells below 200 enabling opportunistic infections
correlates.treatment: Lifelong antiretroviral therapy plus opportunistic infection prophylaxis
correlates.presentation: 30M HIV-positive presents with oral thrush, Pneumocystis pneumonia, and a CD4 count of 80

correlates.name: Air Embolism
correlates.pathophysiology: Air enters vasculature during central line placement, mechanical ventilation, chest wall injury, or surgery; >100 mL needed to obstruct pulmonary circulation
correlates.treatment: Place patient in left lateral decubitus / Trendelenburg; 100% O2; hyperbaric chamber if available
correlates.presentation: Patient develops sudden cardiovascular collapse, neurologic symptoms mimicking stroke, and apnea during central line placement or after a chest wall injury

correlates.name: Albinism
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal recessive tyrosinase defect; melanocytes present but cannot synthesize melanin
correlates.treatment: No cure; rigorous lifelong sun protection and dermatologic surveillance
correlates.presentation: Infant with complete absence of skin and hair pigmentation, white lashes, and nystagmus; tyrosinase deficient

correlates.name: Alpha-thalassemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Deletion of alpha-globin genes on chromosome 16 reduces alpha-chain synthesis
correlates.treatment: Supportive; severe HbH disease may need transfusion; Hb Bart's is lethal
correlates.presentation: Southeast Asian neonate with microcytic anemia and target cells; hemoglobin Bart's on electrophoresis

correlates.name: Amebic Liver Abscess
correlates.pathophysiology: Entamoeba trophozoites invade colon, travel via portal vein, and form necrotic liver abscesses
correlates.treatment: Metronidazole then paromomycin; drainage only if impending rupture
correlates.presentation: 40M returning from Mexico has RUQ pain, fever, and a single right-lobe liver lesion with 'anchovy paste' material

correlates.name: Amniotic Fluid Embolism
correlates.pathophysiology: Amniotic fluid and fetal elements enter maternal circulation via a placental tear; vasoactive substances cause intense pulmonary vasoconstriction and DIC
correlates.treatment: Supportive ICU care; oxygenation, hemodynamic support, transfusions and DIC management
correlates.presentation: Peripartum woman has sudden severe dyspnea, cyanosis, shock, neurologic impairment, and DIC; autopsy shows fetal squamous cells in pulmonary microvasculature

correlates.name: Anemia of chronic disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic inflammation (IL-6) raises hepcidin, locking iron in macrophages
correlates.treatment: Treat the underlying inflammatory disease
correlates.presentation: 60F with rheumatoid arthritis has mild normocytic anemia; high ferritin, low TIBC, low serum iron

correlates.name: Angioedema (ACE-inhibitor)
correlates.pathophysiology: ACE inhibitor blocks bradykinin breakdown causing non-pruritic deep dermal/subcutaneous swelling
correlates.treatment: Stop ACE inhibitor; early intubation if airway threatened; icatibant or ecallantide; antihistamines/steroids ineffective if pure bradykinin-mediated
correlates.presentation: 65F on lisinopril for 1 year develops sudden lip, tongue, and face swelling without urticaria; airway compromise threatening

correlates.name: Antiphospholipid Antibody Syndrome (APS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Autoantibodies (lupus anticoagulant, anticardiolipin, anti-beta-2-glycoprotein I) activate endothelium, monocytes, and platelets, causing arterial and venous thrombosis
correlates.treatment: Long-term anticoagulation (warfarin); LMWH plus aspirin during pregnancy
correlates.presentation: Young woman with recurrent miscarriages, DVT/PE, and stroke; prolonged PTT that fails to correct on mixing study, false-positive RPR, and SLE features

correlates.name: Antithrombin III Deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: Inherited (AD) or acquired deficiency of antithrombin III impairs inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa; characteristic insensitivity to heparin
correlates.treatment: Direct thrombin or Xa inhibitors; warfarin long-term; antithrombin III concentrate; avoid relying on heparin
correlates.presentation: Young adult with recurrent venous thromboses whose PTT fails to prolong appropriately with heparin administration

correlates.name: Aplastic anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Marrow failure with fatty replacement causing pancytopenia
correlates.treatment: Immunosuppression or hematopoietic stem cell transplant
correlates.presentation: 28M with recent benzene exposure has pancytopenia and a hypocellular fatty-replaced marrow biopsy

correlates.name: Aplastic Crisis
correlates.pathophysiology: Parvovirus B19 infection causes temporary RBC production arrest; very low (not necessarily zero) reticulocyte count is the key finding
correlates.treatment: Supportive care (fluids); transfusion if severe
correlates.presentation: 8-year-old with sickle cell disease and recent parvovirus B19 infection has severe anemia and reticulocytopenia

correlates.name: Atheroembolism (Cholesterol Embolism)
correlates.pathophysiology: Atheromatous plaque rupture (often after intra-arterial catheterization) releases cholesterol crystals that lodge in small downstream arteries
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; statins; control cardiovascular risk factors; avoid further instrumentation
correlates.presentation: Older patient after cardiac catheterization develops livedo reticularis, blue toes with palpable pulses, acute kidney injury, and eosinophilia; biopsy shows cholesterol clefts

correlates.name: Atopic Dermatitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Filaggrin mutations and immune dysregulation cause barrier dysfunction and spongiotic dermatitis
correlates.treatment: Emollients, topical corticosteroids, and dupilumab (IL-4/13 inhibitor)
correlates.presentation: 2-year-old with personal and family history of asthma has chronic itchy excoriated plaques in the antecubital fossae

correlates.name: Bacillary Angiomatosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Bartonella infection of vascular endothelium causes proliferative red-purple skin nodules in AIDS
correlates.treatment: Erythromycin or doxycycline
correlates.presentation: 38M with AIDS (CD4 <100) develops red friable vascular papules and nodules on the skin

correlates.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced PTCH1 loss causes constitutive hedgehog pathway activation and basaloid proliferation
correlates.treatment: Surgical excision or Mohs; cryotherapy; topical imiquimod or 5-FU
correlates.presentation: 65M with chronic sun exposure has a pearly papule with telangiectasias and central ulceration on the nose

correlates.name: Behcet Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Idiopathic systemic vasculitis with recurrent oral and genital aphthae, uveitis, and skin lesions
correlates.treatment: Colchicine, topical/systemic corticosteroids, immunosuppressants
correlates.presentation: 30M with recurrent painful oral and genital aphthous ulcers, anterior uveitis with hypopyon, erythema nodosum, and a positive pathergy test 24-48h after needle prick

correlates.name: Bernard-Soulier Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: GpIb deficiency impairs platelet adhesion; giant platelets on smear
correlates.treatment: Platelet transfusion for bleeding
correlates.presentation: Child with mucosal bleeding has giant platelets, prolonged bleeding time, and absent ristocetin aggregation (defective GpIb)

correlates.name: Beta-thalassemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Beta-globin gene mutations on chromosome 11 reduce beta-chain synthesis; elevated HbA2
correlates.treatment: Major: chronic transfusion with iron chelation; minor: none needed
correlates.presentation: Mediterranean child with severe microcytic anemia, hepatosplenomegaly, and frontal bossing; HbA2 elevated

correlates.name: Black-Water Fever
correlates.pathophysiology: Massive intravascular hemolysis in severe malaria causing hemoglobinuria and AKI
correlates.treatment: Supportive care with antimalarial therapy
correlates.presentation: Returning traveler with falciparum malaria develops massive intravascular hemolysis, hemoglobinuria, and acute kidney injury

correlates.name: Blue Nevus
correlates.pathophysiology: Acquired, benign proliferation of deep dermal melanocytes (Tyndall effect produces blue color)
correlates.treatment: Reassurance; excision only if changing or atypical
correlates.presentation: Adult with a 10mm firm, sharply-defined dark-blue to gray-black papule on the dorsum of the hand; stable over years

correlates.name: Bombay phenotype (Oh)
correlates.pathophysiology: Homozygous non-functional H gene means no H-substance, so no A or B antigens form and anti-H is produced
correlates.treatment: Can only receive blood from another Bombay donor
correlates.presentation: Patient typed as group O has a hemolytic transfusion reaction with type O blood; lacks H antigen

correlates.name: Bowen Disease (SCC in situ)
correlates.pathophysiology: Full-thickness epidermal atypia from UV or HPV without dermal invasion; can progress to invasive SCC
correlates.treatment: 5-fluorouracil, imiquimod, cryosurgery, or excision (Mohs)
correlates.presentation: 54F with a sharply demarcated pink-red scaly plaque on the upper back that did not respond to topical hydrocortisone for months

correlates.name: Bullous Pemphigoid
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies against hemidesmosomal BP180 cause subepidermal tense bullae
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids; doxycycline plus niacinamide for milder cases
correlates.presentation: 72F with tense subepidermal bullae on flexural areas; linear IgG at the basement membrane on immunofluorescence

correlates.name: Burkitt lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: t(8;14) overexpresses c-MYC; fastest-growing tumor with starry-sky histology
correlates.treatment: Intensive chemotherapy with tumor lysis prophylaxis (hydration, rasburicase)
correlates.presentation: African child with a rapidly enlarging jaw mass; 'starry-sky' pattern on biopsy and t(8;14) MYC translocation

correlates.name: Burn Injury
correlates.pathophysiology: Thermal, chemical, electrical, or radiation injury causing direct tissue damage with fluid loss and infection risk
correlates.treatment: Cool with water; large burns (>10% TBSA): burn-center transfer, IV fluid resuscitation (Parkland), pain control, topical antimicrobials, possible skin grafting
correlates.presentation: Adult with full-thickness burns on the chest from a kitchen fire; depth ranges from superficial partial-thickness to full-thickness with charred eschar

correlates.name: Cavernous Hemangioma
correlates.pathophysiology: Deep vascular malformation of capillary, lymphatic, and venous tissue (does not involute like infantile hemangioma)
correlates.treatment: Observation; sclerotherapy, laser, or surgical excision if symptomatic
correlates.presentation: Patient with a soft, compressible blue-tinged erythematous nodule that does not regress over time

correlates.name: Cerebral (Severe) Falciparum Malaria
correlates.pathophysiology: Infected RBCs adhere to brain endothelium causing microvascular obstruction and hyperparasitemia
correlates.treatment: IV artesunate, then transition to oral ACT
correlates.presentation: Returning traveler from sub-Saharan Africa with high fever, coma, and seizures; >5% parasitized RBCs

correlates.name: Chagas Cardiomyopathy
correlates.pathophysiology: T. cruzi persists in cardiomyocytes causing chronic immunologic dilated cardiomyopathy with apical aneurysm
correlates.treatment: Benznidazole if early; supportive heart failure/antiarrhythmic care once established
correlates.presentation: 55M from rural Brazil with progressive heart failure, megacolon, and megaesophagus decades after acute infection

correlates.name: Cherry Angioma
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign acquired proliferation of capillaries; first appear around age 30 and increase with age
correlates.treatment: Reassurance; electrodessication or laser for cosmesis
correlates.presentation: 45M with multiple bright red, asymptomatic, dome-shaped papules on the trunk that increase in number over years

correlates.name: Chilblains (Pernio)
correlates.pathophysiology: Intermittent damp non-freezing cold causes inflammatory violaceous nodules
correlates.treatment: Nifedipine plus supportive care; warming and time
correlates.presentation: 30F outdoor worker has tender pruritic violaceous papules on the toes after damp-cold exposure

correlates.name: Chronic Graft-versus-Host Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Donor T cells drive autoimmune-like fibrosing inflammation in skin, mucosae, liver, and lungs beyond 100 days post-BMT
correlates.treatment: Long-term corticosteroids and immunosuppressants; extracorporeal photopheresis
correlates.presentation: Patient >100 days post-BMT has lichen planus-like rash, sclerodermoid skin changes, oral ulcers, and dry eyes

correlates.name: Chronic Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura
correlates.pathophysiology: Autoantibodies (usually against GpIIb/IIIa or GpIb-IX) opsonize platelets for splenic macrophage destruction; primary (idiopathic) or secondary to SLE/HIV/CLL
correlates.treatment: Glucocorticoids; splenectomy for refractory cases (normalizes count in ~2/3); IVIG for acute flares
correlates.presentation: Adult woman with insidious onset of mucocutaneous bleeding, petechiae, easy bruising, epistaxis, and menorrhagia; isolated thrombocytopenia with otherwise normal blood counts and PT/PTT

correlates.name: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL)
correlates.pathophysiology: Accumulation of fragile mature B cells; smudge cells and hypogammaglobulinemia
correlates.treatment: BTK inhibitors (ibrutinib); watch-and-wait if asymptomatic
correlates.presentation: 70M with incidental lymphocytosis >5000 and smudge cells on smear; otherwise asymptomatic

correlates.name: Chronic myelogenous leukemia (CML)
correlates.pathophysiology: Philadelphia chromosome t(9;22) creates the constitutively active BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase
correlates.treatment: Imatinib or other BCR-ABL tyrosine kinase inhibitors
correlates.presentation: 50F with massive splenomegaly, fatigue, and leukocytosis with left shift; BCR-ABL t(9;22) positive

correlates.name: Cirrhosis Cutaneous Stigmata
correlates.pathophysiology: Hepatic dysfunction causes hyperestrogenemia, vascular dilation, and impaired clotting/protein synthesis
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying liver disease; transplant if end-stage
correlates.presentation: 55M with alcohol use disorder has jaundice, palmar erythema, spider telangiectasias on the upper trunk, and Terry nails (proximal 2/3 white)

correlates.name: Congenital Melanocytic Nevus
correlates.pathophysiology: Nevus present at birth; giant nevi (>20 cm) have 3-8% lifetime melanoma risk
correlates.treatment: Small: observe; giant: prophylactic excision and lifelong surveillance
correlates.presentation: 55M with a 1 cm hairy pigmented lesion present since birth that has not changed; small lesions carry baseline melanoma risk but giant lesions warrant excision

correlates.name: Congenital Rubella Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Maternal rubella infection in pregnancy disrupts fetal organogenesis via cell apoptosis
correlates.treatment: Prevent with pre-pregnancy MMR; supportive care for hearing, eye, cardiac defects
correlates.presentation: Newborn of unvaccinated mother with sensorineural deafness, cataracts, and patent ductus arteriosus

correlates.name: Cowden Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal dominant PTEN mutation causing multiple hamartomas and increased risk of breast, thyroid, and endometrial cancer
correlates.treatment: Cancer surveillance (breast, thyroid, endometrium); excise symptomatic lesions
correlates.presentation: 30F with warty papules (trichilemmomas) on the face and forearms, oral cobblestone papules, GI polyps, and a strong family history of breast cancer

correlates.name: Cryptococcal Meningitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Inhaled encapsulated yeast disseminates from lungs to CNS in HIV patients with CD4 under 100
correlates.treatment: Induction with liposomal amphotericin B + flucytosine, then fluconazole
correlates.presentation: AIDS patient with subacute headache, fever, and altered mental status; India ink shows encapsulated yeast in CSF

correlates.name: Cutaneous Candidiasis
correlates.pathophysiology: Candida albicans overgrowth in warm, moist, occluded skin folds; predisposed by diabetes, obesity, immunosuppression
correlates.treatment: Topical nystatin or azole antifungals; treat predisposing factors
correlates.presentation: Obese diabetic with a beefy-red intertriginous eruption with satellite pustules beyond the border and maceration of skin folds; KOH shows budding yeast and pseudohyphae

correlates.name: Decompression Sickness
correlates.pathophysiology: Rapid ascent causes dissolved nitrogen to form gas bubbles in tissues, joints, and vasculature; chronic form (Caisson disease) causes avascular necrosis
correlates.treatment: Immediate 100% O2 and hyperbaric recompression therapy
correlates.presentation: SCUBA diver after rapid ascent has joint pain (the bends), respiratory distress (the chokes), neurologic symptoms, and skin mottling

correlates.name: Deep Vein Thrombosis (DVT)
correlates.pathophysiology: Virchow triad (stasis, endothelial injury, hypercoagulability) drives thrombus in deep leg veins; ~90% in lower extremities
correlates.treatment: Anticoagulation (LMWH bridge to warfarin or DOAC); IVC filter if anticoagulation contraindicated
correlates.presentation: Post-op or immobilized patient develops unilateral calf swelling, pain, warmth, and a positive Homans sign; compression ultrasound is diagnostic

correlates.name: Dengue Hemorrhagic Fever
correlates.pathophysiology: Antibody-dependent enhancement on a second dengue serotype boosts viral entry and inflammation
correlates.treatment: Aggressive supportive fluid management
correlates.presentation: Returning traveler with second dengue infection has high fever, plasma leakage, thrombocytopenia, and shock

correlates.name: Dermatitis Herpetiformis
correlates.pathophysiology: IgA against tissue transglutaminase deposits at dermal papillary tips; linked to celiac disease
correlates.treatment: Strict gluten-free diet plus dapsone for rapid relief
correlates.presentation: 30M with celiac disease has intensely pruritic grouped vesicles on the elbows and knees; granular IgA at dermal papillae

correlates.name: Dermatofibroma
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign fibrohistiocytic proliferation; thought to be a reactive response to trauma or insect bite
correlates.treatment: Reassurance; excision only for cosmesis
correlates.presentation: 33F with a firm, dome-shaped 5mm hyperpigmented papule on the leg after shaving; lateral compression produces the 'dimple sign'

correlates.name: Dermatomyositis
correlates.pathophysiology: Humoral autoimmune attack on perimysial capillaries causing muscle ischemia
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids, methotrexate/azathioprine; screen for occult malignancy
correlates.presentation: 50F with proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope eyelid rash, and Gottron papules; elevated CK and anti-Mi-2

correlates.name: Dermatosis Papulosa Nigra
correlates.pathophysiology: Variant of seborrheic keratosis seen in darkly pigmented patients
correlates.treatment: Snip excision, electrodessication, or laser for cosmesis
correlates.presentation: 40F African-American with multiple tiny, asymptomatic black papules scattered on the cheeks and temples

correlates.name: Diamond-Blackfan anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Congenital pure red cell aplasia with intrinsic ribosomal defect
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids; transfusion support
correlates.presentation: Infant with severe macrocytic anemia, craniofacial anomalies, and triphalangeal thumbs; pure red cell aplasia

correlates.name: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)
correlates.pathophysiology: Most common adult NHL; rapidly enlarging mass, often extranodal, may arise de novo or from transformation
correlates.treatment: R-CHOP; CAR-T for relapsed disease
correlates.presentation: 60M with a rapidly enlarging cervical lymph node mass; large CD20+ B cells on biopsy

correlates.name: Discoid Lupus Erythematosus
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic cutaneous lupus with interface dermatitis, follicular plugging, and scarring; only ~5% progress to SLE
correlates.treatment: Sun protection, topical/intralesional steroids, antimalarials (hydroxychloroquine)
correlates.presentation: 35F has sharply defined erythematous scaly plaques with follicular plugging and 'carpet-tack' scale on the scalp and face causing scarring alopecia

correlates.name: Disorders of Fibrinolysis (Plasmin Overactivity)
correlates.pathophysiology: Plasmin overactivity (urokinase release after radical prostatectomy, or reduced alpha-2-antiplasmin in cirrhosis) excessively cleaves fibrinogen and inactivates clotting factors
correlates.treatment: Aminocaproic acid (blocks plasminogen activation)
correlates.presentation: Cirrhotic or post-radical-prostatectomy patient with bleeding, prolonged PT/PTT and bleeding time, normal platelet count, elevated fibrin split products but no D-dimer (no fibrin thrombi)

correlates.name: Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC)
correlates.pathophysiology: Widespread activation of coagulation consumes clotting factors and platelets
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying cause; FFP, cryoprecipitate, and platelet support
correlates.presentation: 65F with sepsis develops oozing from IV sites; prolonged PT/PTT, low platelets, high D-dimer, low fibrinogen

correlates.name: DRESS Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Delayed type IV drug hypersensitivity with eosinophilia and visceral organ injury
correlates.treatment: Withdraw offending drug; ICU support; long corticosteroid taper
correlates.presentation: 30F started on phenytoin 4 weeks ago has fever, diffuse rash, lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia, and hepatitis

correlates.name: Drug-Induced Lupus
correlates.pathophysiology: Anti-histone antibodies induced by certain drugs (HIP: Hydralazine, Isoniazid, Procainamide); resolves on drug withdrawal
correlates.treatment: Stop offending drug; NSAIDs or low-dose steroids for symptoms
correlates.presentation: 65M on hydralazine develops arthralgias, malar rash, and serositis; anti-histone antibodies positive, anti-dsDNA negative

correlates.name: Dysplastic Nevus
correlates.pathophysiology: BRAF/NRAS mutation plus CDKN2A loss producing cytologic atypia and architectural disorder
correlates.treatment: Monitor; excise concerning lesions; surveillance if familial syndrome
correlates.presentation: 30M with family history of melanoma has an asymmetric pigmented lesion >6 mm with variegated color and irregular borders

correlates.name: Erythema Multiforme
correlates.pathophysiology: Type IV interface reaction, most often triggered by HSV, producing targetoid lesions
correlates.treatment: Treat the trigger (suppressive acyclovir for HSV); supportive care
correlates.presentation: 20M with a recent HSV outbreak has target lesions on the palms and extensor surfaces

correlates.name: Erythema Nodosum
correlates.pathophysiology: Septal panniculitis; hypersensitivity reaction to strep, sarcoidosis, IBD, or drugs
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying cause; NSAIDs for pain
correlates.presentation: 30F with sarcoidosis has tender erythematous nodules on the anterior shins

correlates.name: Erythrasma
correlates.pathophysiology: Superficial bacterial skin infection by Corynebacterium minutissimum; predisposed by sweating, obesity, diabetes
correlates.treatment: Topical or oral erythromycin; topical clindamycin
correlates.presentation: 50M with brown, well-demarcated patches in the groin and axillae; Wood lamp shows coral-red fluorescence from porphyrins

correlates.name: Ewing Sarcoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Primitive neuroectodermal tumor with t(11;22) EWSR1-FLI1 fusion; small round blue cells in long-bone diaphysis
correlates.treatment: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy, surgical resection, and radiation
correlates.presentation: Caucasian adolescent with progressively worsening diaphyseal long-bone pain (worse at night), fever, leukocytosis, and an onion-skin periosteal reaction on x-ray

correlates.name: Extramedullary hematopoiesis
correlates.pathophysiology: Failing bone marrow shifts blood cell production back to embryonic sites: liver, spleen, and lymph nodes
correlates.treatment: Treat underlying cause (e.g., myelofibrosis); supportive transfusion
correlates.presentation: Patient with chronic hemolysis has hepatosplenomegaly and paraspinal masses on imaging

correlates.name: Factor V Leiden
correlates.pathophysiology: Mutant factor V resists inactivation by activated protein C, causing hypercoagulability
correlates.treatment: Anticoagulation after a thrombotic event
correlates.presentation: 30F with unprovoked DVT and family history of clotting; activated protein C resistance on testing

correlates.name: Fanconi anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Inherited defect in DNA cross-link repair causing pancytopenia
correlates.treatment: Hematopoietic stem cell transplant; supportive care
correlates.presentation: 8-year-old of short stature with café-au-lait spots, absent thumbs, and pancytopenia; chromosomal breakage on DEB test

correlates.name: Fat Embolism Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Marrow fat enters circulation after long bone fracture
correlates.treatment: Supportive respiratory care
correlates.presentation: 25M 24-72 hours after a long-bone fracture has hypoxia, confusion, and a petechial rash on the chest/axillae

correlates.name: Follicular lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: t(14;18) overexpresses anti-apoptotic BCL-2, so cells refuse to die
correlates.treatment: Watch-and-wait; rituximab-based therapy when symptomatic
correlates.presentation: 60M with painless waxing and waning lymphadenopathy; t(14;18) BCL2 translocation in CD10+ B cells

correlates.name: Frostbite
correlates.pathophysiology: Tissue freezing forms ice crystals; rewarming triggers microvascular thrombosis
correlates.treatment: Rapid rewarming in 37-39 C water; analgesia, tetanus, thrombolytics if severe
correlates.presentation: 30M ice climber with white, waxy, anesthetic fingers after prolonged cold exposure; blisters form on rewarming

correlates.name: G6PD deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: Lack of NADPH leaves RBCs vulnerable to oxidative stress, denaturing hemoglobin into Heinz bodies
correlates.treatment: Avoid oxidant triggers (fava beans, sulfa drugs); supportive care
correlates.presentation: African-American male develops hemolytic anemia after antimalarial therapy; Heinz bodies and bite cells on smear

correlates.name: Gardner Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal dominant APC mutation; variant of familial adenomatous polyposis with extracolonic manifestations
correlates.treatment: Prophylactic colectomy; excision of symptomatic cysts/osteomas
correlates.presentation: 20M with >100 adenomatous colonic polyps, multiple epidermal cysts on the face/scalp, mandibular osteomas, and supernumerary teeth

correlates.name: Glanzmann Thrombasthenia
correlates.pathophysiology: GpIIb/IIIa deficiency prevents platelet aggregation
correlates.treatment: Platelet transfusion for bleeding
correlates.presentation: Child with mucocutaneous bleeding and normal platelet count; absent platelet aggregation to all agonists except ristocetin

correlates.name: Guttate Psoriasis
correlates.pathophysiology: Acute psoriasis variant triggered by streptococcal pharyngitis with diffuse small papules
correlates.treatment: Treat strep if active; topical steroids, UVB phototherapy; usually self-limited
correlates.presentation: 15M develops a generalized eruption of 1-2 cm scaly salmon-pink 'teardrop' papules sparing palms and soles, 5 days after strep pharyngitis; ASO titer elevated

correlates.name: Halo Nevus
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign nevus surrounded by a depigmented halo from T-cell-mediated regression of central melanocytes
correlates.treatment: Reassurance; excise only if central lesion is atypical
correlates.presentation: Adolescent with a pre-existing nevus surrounded by a ring of depigmentation; the central nevus often involutes over months to years

correlates.name: Heat Exhaustion
correlates.pathophysiology: Heat-related volume and electrolyte depletion with preserved mental status
correlates.treatment: Cool environment, leg elevation, oral or IV fluid/electrolyte replacement
correlates.presentation: Marathon runner has fatigue, headache, nausea, and temperature 39°C with intact mental status

correlates.name: Heat Stroke
correlates.pathophysiology: Core temperature above 40 C causes protein denaturation and multi-organ failure
correlates.treatment: Aggressive evaporative cooling, IV fluids, ICU; antipyretics are useless
correlates.presentation: Football player collapses with core temperature 41°C, altered mental status, and (classic) anhidrosis

correlates.name: Hemolytic disease of the fetus and newborn (HDFN)
correlates.pathophysiology: Sensitized Rh-negative mother makes IgG anti-D that crosses the placenta to destroy fetal Rh+ RBCs
correlates.treatment: RhoGAM prophylaxis; in utero or exchange transfusion plus phototherapy
correlates.presentation: Newborn of an Rh-negative mother with prior Rh+ pregnancy has hemolytic anemia, jaundice, and hydrops fetalis

correlates.name: Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (HUS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Shiga-like toxin from E. coli O157:H7 injures endothelium causing renal microthrombi
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; dialysis as needed
correlates.presentation: 5-year-old with bloody diarrhea after undercooked beef develops hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and acute kidney injury

correlates.name: Hemophilia
correlates.pathophysiology: X-linked deficiency of factor VIII (A) or factor IX (B) impairs secondary hemostasis
correlates.treatment: Factor replacement (VIII or IX)
correlates.presentation: Male infant with prolonged bleeding after circumcision and hemarthroses; prolonged PTT, normal PT and platelets

correlates.name: Hemorrhagic Disease of the Newborn
correlates.pathophysiology: Newborn vitamin K stores are low (poor placental transfer, sterile gut, immature liver) so vitamin K-dependent factors II/VII/IX/X are inadequate
correlates.treatment: Prophylactic vitamin K IM at birth; vitamin K replacement and FFP for active bleeding
correlates.presentation: Home-birth newborn who did not receive vitamin K presents at 1-12 weeks with bleeding from the umbilicus, GI tract, or an intracranial hemorrhage; prolonged PT with normal PTT and platelets

correlates.name: Henoch-Schonlein Purpura (IgA Vasculitis)
correlates.pathophysiology: IgA immune complex deposition in small vessel walls causing leukocytoclastic vasculitis after viral URI or strep infection
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; corticosteroids for severe abdominal or renal disease
correlates.presentation: Child after a URI with palpable purpura on the buttocks and lower extremities, colicky abdominal pain, polyarthralgia, and hematuria from IgA nephropathy

correlates.name: Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia (HIT)
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG against heparin-PF4 complexes activates platelets causing thrombosis and low counts
correlates.treatment: Stop heparin; start a direct thrombin inhibitor (argatroban)
correlates.presentation: Post-op patient on heparin >5 days has a 50% platelet drop and new arterial or venous thrombosis

correlates.name: Hereditary Angioedema
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal dominant C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency causing unopposed bradykinin and angioedema
correlates.treatment: C1 inhibitor concentrate, ecallantide, or icatibant (not antihistamines)
correlates.presentation: 20F with recurrent non-pruritic face and lip swelling plus abdominal pain; low C4 and C1 esterase inhibitor deficiency

correlates.name: Hereditary Hemorrhagic Telangiectasia (Osler-Weber-Rendu)
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal dominant defect (ENG, ACVRL1) causing telangiectasias and AVMs of skin, mucosae, and viscera
correlates.treatment: Iron supplementation; embolization of visceral AVMs; laser/cautery for epistaxis
correlates.presentation: 40M with recurrent epistaxis, mucocutaneous telangiectasias of the lips/tongue/fingertips, GI bleeding, and a first-degree relative with the same

correlates.name: Hereditary spherocytosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Defects in ankyrin, spectrin, or band 3 cause membrane loss and rigid spheres trapped in the spleen
correlates.treatment: Splenectomy
correlates.presentation: Northern European child with anemia, jaundice, and splenomegaly; spherocytes on smear and positive osmotic fragility

correlates.name: Herpes Zoster (Shingles)
correlates.pathophysiology: Reactivation of latent VZV in a dorsal root or cranial nerve ganglion
correlates.treatment: Acyclovir/valacyclovir within 72 hours; Shingrix vaccine for prevention
correlates.presentation: 70M with painful unilateral vesicular eruption in a single thoracic dermatome

correlates.name: Herpes Zoster Ophthalmicus
correlates.pathophysiology: Reactivation of latent VZV in the trigeminal ganglion affecting the V1 ophthalmic branch; can threaten vision
correlates.treatment: Urgent ophthalmology consult; oral acyclovir/valacyclovir; topical corticosteroids for keratitis
correlates.presentation: 70F with unilateral forehead vesicular rash respecting the midline, eye pain, and lesions on the nose tip (Hutchinson sign predicting ocular involvement)

correlates.name: Hodgkin lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+/CD30+) secrete cytokines summoning a reactive infiltrate; contiguous nodal spread
