correlates.treatment: ABVD chemotherapy
correlates.presentation: 20M with painless cervical lymphadenopathy, B symptoms, and Reed-Sternberg cells (CD15+/CD30+) on biopsy

correlates.name: Hyperhomocysteinemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Deficiency of cystathione beta-synthase or of B6/B12/folate elevates homocysteine, damaging endothelium and promoting arterial and venous thrombosis
correlates.treatment: B6, B12, and folate supplementation; treat underlying cause
correlates.presentation: Young adult with premature atherosclerosis, recurrent thromboses, marfanoid habitus, lens dislocation, and elevated serum homocysteine

correlates.name: Hyperleukocytosis
correlates.pathophysiology: WBC >100,000/uL in acute leukemia causes leukocyte aggregates (white thrombi) that occlude pulmonary and CNS microvasculature
correlates.treatment: Aggressive hydration, leukapheresis, urgent induction chemotherapy; manage tumor lysis prophylactically
correlates.presentation: Newly diagnosed leukemia patient with WBC >100,000 develops dyspnea, hypoxia, headache, mental status changes, and visual disturbances from leukostasis

correlates.name: Immune Reconstitution Inflammatory Syndrome (IRIS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Rising CD4 count after starting ART triggers a violent inflammatory response to existing pathogen burden
correlates.treatment: Delay ART 2-4 weeks after treating the opportunistic infection
correlates.presentation: AIDS patient 2-12 weeks after starting ART has paradoxical worsening of an existing opportunistic infection

correlates.name: Immune Thrombocytopenic Purpura (ITP)
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies against GpIIb/IIIa drive splenic macrophage destruction of platelets
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids, IVIG; splenectomy in refractory cases
correlates.presentation: 5-year-old with petechiae and isolated thrombocytopenia 1-3 weeks after a viral illness; marrow normal

correlates.name: Infantile Hemangioma (Strawberry Nevus)
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign vascular tumor with rapid proliferation in the first year followed by spontaneous involution by age 5-10
correlates.treatment: Observation; propranolol for ulcerating, large, or vital-structure lesions
correlates.presentation: 6-month-old with a rapidly growing bright red strawberry-appearing plaque on the trunk; expected to involute by age 5

correlates.name: Inhalation Anthrax (Woolsorter's Disease)
correlates.pathophysiology: Inhaled spores germinate in mediastinal nodes, releasing tripartite toxin causing hemorrhagic mediastinitis
correlates.treatment: IV ciprofloxacin/doxycycline + clindamycin + additional agent; raxibacumab
correlates.presentation: Woolsorter develops a flu-like illness progressing to mediastinal widening, hemorrhagic mediastinitis, and shock

correlates.name: Intertrigo
correlates.pathophysiology: Inflammatory eruption of opposing skin surfaces from moisture, friction, and maceration; often secondarily infected
correlates.treatment: Keep folds dry; barrier creams; treat superinfection (candida or bacterial)
correlates.presentation: Obese patient with well-demarcated mirror-image erythematous patches in the axillary, inframammary, and inguinal folds; KOH/culture rule out fungal/candidal etiology

correlates.name: Inverse Psoriasis
correlates.pathophysiology: Psoriasis localized to intertriginous areas; lacks typical scale because of moisture
correlates.treatment: Low-potency topical steroids, calcineurin inhibitors; avoid friction
correlates.presentation: 40M with deep-pink well-demarcated plaques in the axillae, inframammary folds, and inguinal creases including penis and scrotum; KOH negative

correlates.name: Iron deficiency anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Iron loss or increased demand outpaces intake, depleting stores for hemoglobin synthesis
correlates.treatment: Oral ferrous sulfate; identify and treat the bleeding source
correlates.presentation: 30F with heavy menses has microcytic hypochromic anemia, low ferritin, high TIBC, low serum iron, and pica

correlates.name: Kawasaki Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Medium-vessel vasculitis of childhood causing coronary artery aneurysms
correlates.treatment: IVIG plus high-dose aspirin; echocardiogram after diagnosis
correlates.presentation: 4-year-old with fever >5 days, conjunctivitis, strawberry tongue, polymorphous rash, and cervical lymphadenopathy

correlates.name: Klippel-Trenaunay-Weber Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Congenital capillary-lymphatic-venous malformation with limb overgrowth
correlates.treatment: Compression, sclerotherapy, laser; orthopedic management of leg-length discrepancy
correlates.presentation: Child with an extensive port-wine stain on a single extremity, varicose veins, and ipsilateral soft-tissue/bone hypertrophy

correlates.name: Kwashiorkor
correlates.pathophysiology: Severe protein malnutrition with preserved or excess caloric intake causing hypoalbuminemic edema
correlates.treatment: Cautious refeeding with protein; treat infections and electrolyte derangements
correlates.presentation: Child in famine with distended abdomen, peripheral pitting edema, depigmented hair bands ('flag sign'), and peeling 'enamel paint' dermatosis

correlates.name: Lead poisoning
correlates.pathophysiology: Lead inhibits ALAD and ferrochelatase, impairing heme synthesis; basophilic stippling appears
correlates.treatment: Chelation (e.g., succimer, EDTA, dimercaprol)
correlates.presentation: 5-year-old in old housing has abdominal pain, microcytic anemia with basophilic stippling, and elevated blood lead

correlates.name: Lichen Planus
correlates.pathophysiology: CD8+ T-cell attack on basal keratinocytes; associated with hepatitis C
correlates.treatment: Topical corticosteroids; self-limited over months to years
correlates.presentation: Adult with pruritic flat-topped polygonal violaceous papules on the wrists and Wickham striae on oral mucosa

correlates.name: Lichen Simplex Chronicus
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic itch-scratch cycle in atopic individuals causes lichenified plaques
correlates.treatment: Break the itch-scratch cycle; high-potency topical steroids; antihistamines
correlates.presentation: 45F with atopic history has a solitary thickened lichenified plaque on the scrotum/wrist/posterior neck that she scratches repeatedly

correlates.name: Mantle cell lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: t(11;14) overexpresses cyclin D1, pushing cells past the G1/S checkpoint; CD5+/CD23-
correlates.treatment: Chemoimmunotherapy; BTK inhibitors
correlates.presentation: 60M with disseminated lymphadenopathy and GI involvement; cyclin D1+ B cells with t(11;14)

correlates.name: Measles (Rubeola)
correlates.pathophysiology: Single-stranded RNA paramyxovirus transmitted by respiratory droplets; highly contagious
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; vitamin A reduces morbidity/mortality; prevention via MMR vaccine
correlates.presentation: Unvaccinated child with fever and 4 C's (cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, Koplik spots) followed by a cephalocaudal maculopapular rash; complications include encephalitis and SSPE years later

correlates.name: Megaloblastic anemia (B12/folate deficiency)
correlates.pathophysiology: Impaired DNA synthesis from B12 or folate deficiency causes large cells and hypersegmented neutrophils
correlates.treatment: Replace the deficient vitamin; confirm B12 status before giving folate
correlates.presentation: 70M strict vegan with macrocytic anemia, hypersegmented neutrophils, and paresthesias from B12 deficiency

correlates.name: Melanoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant melanocyte transformation from UV-induced DNA damage and BRAF V600E mutations
correlates.treatment: Wide local excision by Breslow depth; immunotherapy and BRAF/MEK inhibitors for advanced disease
correlates.presentation: 40M with a changing pigmented lesion meeting ABCDE criteria; biopsy shows atypical melanocytes invading >1 mm

correlates.name: Milium
correlates.pathophysiology: Superficial keratin-containing epidermal cyst arising spontaneously or post-trauma
correlates.treatment: Incision and expression of contents
correlates.presentation: 30F with multiple 1-2mm pearly white papules on the eyelids and cheeks

correlates.name: Morphea (Localized Scleroderma)
correlates.pathophysiology: Localized fibrosis confined to skin and subcutaneous tissue without systemic sclerosis features
correlates.treatment: Topical/intralesional steroids; phototherapy; methotrexate for generalized disease
correlates.presentation: 30F with violaceous-to-ivory indurated plaques on the trunk; linear variant 'en coup de sabre' on the forehead; no Raynaud or organ involvement

correlates.name: Multiple myeloma
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant plasma cell clone produces an M-spike causing CRAB (hypercalcemia, renal failure, anemia, lytic bone lesions)
correlates.treatment: Lenalidomide + bortezomib + dexamethasone (RVd)
correlates.presentation: 65M with bone pain, fatigue, hypercalcemia, renal failure, and M-spike on SPEP; rouleaux on smear

correlates.name: Mycosis Fungoides
correlates.pathophysiology: Cutaneous T-cell lymphoma; clonal CD4+ T-cell proliferation in skin progressing through patch, plaque, and tumor stages
correlates.treatment: Topical steroids, phototherapy (PUVA), localized radiation; advanced disease: systemic therapy
correlates.presentation: 60M with chronic patches, plaques, and tumors in non-sun-exposed areas, often misdiagnosed for years as eczema or psoriasis; biopsy shows Pautrier microabscesses

correlates.name: Necrotizing Fasciitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Rapid bacterial invasion of deep fascial planes with proteases, thrombosis, and tissue necrosis
correlates.treatment: Emergent surgical debridement plus broad-spectrum IV antibiotics
correlates.presentation: Diabetic with rapidly spreading erythema, pain out of proportion to exam, crepitus, and systemic toxicity

correlates.name: Neuroblastoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant tumor of primordial neural crest cells of the sympathetic chain or adrenal medulla; N-myc amplification confers poor prognosis
correlates.treatment: Risk-stratified surgery, chemotherapy, radiation, and immunotherapy (anti-GD2); observation for low-risk infants
correlates.presentation: Child under 5 with an abdominal mass crossing the midline, opsoclonus-myoclonus (dancing eyes, dancing feet), secretory diarrhea (VIP), elevated urine HVA/VMA, and Homer-Wright rosettes on biopsy

correlates.name: Nevirapine Hepatotoxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: Hypersensitivity-mediated hepatocellular injury, worse with higher CD4 counts
correlates.treatment: Stop nevirapine immediately and permanently; supportive care
correlates.presentation: HIV patient started on nevirapine has fever, rash, and severe hepatitis within the first 6 weeks

correlates.name: Nevus Spilus
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign light-brown background macule speckled with darker macules/papules (junctional nevi)
correlates.treatment: Reassurance; excise atypical components
correlates.presentation: Child with a light brown patch on the trunk speckled with multiple small darker brown macules and papules within the pigmented background

correlates.name: NRTI Lactic Acidosis with Hepatic Steatosis
correlates.pathophysiology: NRTI inhibition of mitochondrial DNA polymerase gamma impairs oxidative phosphorylation
correlates.treatment: Discontinue NRTI immediately; supportive care for lactate clearance
correlates.presentation: HIV patient on long-term NRTI therapy has nausea, abdominal pain, hepatomegaly, and severe lactic acidosis

correlates.name: Onychomycosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Dermatophyte (most often Trichophyton rubrum) infection of the nail; subtypes: distal-lateral subungual, superficial white, proximal subungual (HIV-associated)
correlates.treatment: Oral terbinafine or itraconazole; confirm with KOH/culture before systemic therapy
correlates.presentation: 55M with thickened, yellow, crumbly toenails with subungual debris; KOH shows septate branching hyphae

correlates.name: Osteosarcoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Malignant osteoblastic tumor associated with Rb and TP53 (Li-Fraumeni) mutations; metaphysis of long bones at the knee
correlates.treatment: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy and limb-salvage surgical resection
correlates.presentation: Adolescent in a growth spurt with persistent worsening knee pain and swelling; x-ray of the distal femur shows a sunburst pattern with Codman triangle

correlates.name: Paradoxical Embolism
correlates.pathophysiology: Venous thrombus crosses to the arterial circulation through a patent foramen ovale or septal defect
correlates.treatment: Anticoagulation; closure of the intracardiac shunt
correlates.presentation: Young patient with a DVT presents with an unexplained ischemic stroke; bubble-study echocardiogram demonstrates a right-to-left shunt

correlates.name: Paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria (PNH)
correlates.pathophysiology: Acquired PIGA mutation removes GPI-anchored CD55/CD59, leaving RBCs defenseless against complement
correlates.treatment: Eculizumab (anti-C5)
correlates.presentation: Adult with episodic dark morning urine, thrombosis at unusual sites, and pancytopenia; CD55/CD59 deficient by flow

correlates.name: Pellagra
correlates.pathophysiology: Niacin (vitamin B3) deficiency from inadequate intake, carcinoid, isoniazid, or Hartnup disease
correlates.treatment: Oral nicotinamide; treat underlying cause
correlates.presentation: Alcoholic with the 3 D's: dermatitis (erythematous photodistributed rash including 'Casal necklace'), diarrhea, and dementia

correlates.name: Pemphigus Vulgaris
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies against desmoglein 3 cause suprabasal acantholysis and flaccid bullae
correlates.treatment: Systemic corticosteroids plus rituximab or other immunosuppressants
correlates.presentation: 50F with painful flaccid bullae and oral erosions; positive Nikolsky sign and anti-desmoglein 3 antibodies

correlates.name: Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal dominant STK11 mutation causing hamartomatous GI polyps with increased GI and non-GI cancer risk
correlates.treatment: Endoscopic surveillance from childhood; cancer screening (breast, pancreatic, ovarian)
correlates.presentation: 20M with intussusception from small-bowel hamartomatous polyps and characteristic dark macules on the lips, oral mucosa, and perioral region

correlates.name: Physiologic Anemia of Infancy (Physiologic Nadir)
correlates.pathophysiology: Postnatal rise in tissue oxygenation downregulates EPO, suppressing erythropoiesis until levels self-correct around 6-8 weeks
correlates.treatment: No treatment needed; reassurance and follow-up
correlates.presentation: Healthy 2-month-old infant has a hemoglobin of 10-11 g/dL on routine labs with normal WBC and platelet counts and no red flags

correlates.name: Pityriasis Rosea
correlates.pathophysiology: Self-limited eruption, likely HHV-6/7, with a herald patch then Christmas-tree truncal rash
correlates.treatment: Supportive; self-resolves over 6-8 weeks
correlates.presentation: 20F with a single 'herald patch' followed by oval scaly plaques in a 'Christmas tree' distribution on the trunk

correlates.name: Plummer-Vinson syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Iron deficiency anemia associated with esophageal webs and atrophic glossitis
correlates.treatment: Iron repletion; dilation of esophageal webs if needed
correlates.presentation: Middle-aged woman with iron deficiency anemia, dysphagia, and esophageal webs; increased risk of esophageal SCC

correlates.name: Port-Wine Stain (Nevus Flammeus)
correlates.pathophysiology: Capillary malformation present at birth that does not involute; somatic GNAQ mutation
correlates.treatment: Pulsed-dye laser; evaluate for Sturge-Weber if V1 distribution
correlates.presentation: Infant with a unilateral red-violaceous patch in a dermatomal distribution that does not cross the midline and does not regress; persists and darkens with age

correlates.name: Protease Inhibitor Lipodystrophy
correlates.pathophysiology: PIs impair GLUT4 glucose uptake and adipocyte differentiation via SREBP interference
correlates.treatment: Switch to non-PI regimen; CYP-safe statins; metformin; diet and exercise
correlates.presentation: HIV patient on protease inhibitors has central fat accumulation, facial wasting, dyslipidemia, and insulin resistance

correlates.name: Protein C or S Deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: Deficient vitamin K-dependent anticoagulants cannot inactivate factors Va and VIIIa; warfarin transiently worsens this by dropping protein C first (skin necrosis)
correlates.treatment: Heparin bridge when starting warfarin; long-term anticoagulation; protein C concentrate in severe deficiency
correlates.presentation: Young adult with recurrent DVTs starting in adolescence; develops painful skin necrosis on the trunk shortly after warfarin is initiated

correlates.name: Prothrombin Gene Mutation (G20210A)
correlates.pathophysiology: G20210A single-nucleotide variant in the 3' UTR raises prothrombin levels and 3-fold increases venous thrombosis risk
correlates.treatment: Anticoagulation for thrombotic events; lifestyle and OCP avoidance; long-term anticoagulation if recurrent
correlates.presentation: Young adult with unprovoked DVT or PE and a family history of clots; genetic testing reveals the G20210A prothrombin variant

correlates.name: Psoriasis
correlates.pathophysiology: Th17-driven keratinocyte hyperproliferation with maturation accelerated to 8-10 days
correlates.treatment: Topical steroids and vitamin D analogs, phototherapy, biologics for severe disease
correlates.presentation: 30M with well-demarcated erythematous plaques and silvery scales on the extensor surfaces; Auspitz sign positive

correlates.name: Psoriasis Vulgaris
correlates.pathophysiology: Th17-mediated chronic immune-mediated skin disease with hyperproliferation and impaired keratinocyte differentiation
correlates.treatment: Topical steroids and vitamin D analogs; phototherapy; methotrexate, biologics (anti-TNF, anti-IL-17/23) for severe disease
correlates.presentation: 27F with thick silvery-white scaly plaques on the scalp, elbows, knees, and lower back; nail pitting and oil spots; pinpoint bleeding when scale is scraped (Auspitz sign); family history positive

correlates.name: Pulmonary Embolism
correlates.pathophysiology: Embolized DVT lodges in the pulmonary arteries; saddle embolus causes sudden death
correlates.treatment: Anticoagulation; thrombolysis for massive PE
correlates.presentation: Post-op patient has sudden dyspnea, pleuritic chest pain, tachycardia, and hypoxia; positive CT pulmonary angiogram

correlates.name: Pyogenic Granuloma
correlates.pathophysiology: Reactive, rapidly proliferating capillary growth at sites of minor trauma; also pregnancy
correlates.treatment: Surgical excision with electrodessication of the base; recurs if incompletely removed
correlates.presentation: 24M construction worker with a rapidly growing bright red dome-shaped friable nodule on the finger that bleeds spontaneously after a minor injury

correlates.name: Ramsay Hunt Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Herpes zoster reactivation in the geniculate ganglion involving cranial nerve VIII
correlates.treatment: Acyclovir plus corticosteroids
correlates.presentation: 60M with facial palsy, vesicles in the external auditory canal, and ipsilateral hearing loss from VZV reactivation

correlates.name: Relapsing Polychondritis
correlates.pathophysiology: Immune-mediated recurrent inflammation of cartilage (ears, nose, joints, tracheobronchial tree, eyes)
correlates.treatment: NSAIDs for mild disease; corticosteroids; immunosuppressants for severe disease
correlates.presentation: 50M with recurrent tender erythematous swollen auricles that spare the lobule, saddle-nose deformity, and arthritis; may have aortic insufficiency

correlates.name: Retinoblastoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Biallelic inactivation of the RB1 tumor suppressor (two-hit hypothesis); hereditary form is bilateral and increases osteosarcoma risk
correlates.treatment: Enucleation if vision cannot be saved; chemoreduction with focal laser or cryotherapy for salvageable eyes
correlates.presentation: Toddler with leukocoria (white pupillary reflex), strabismus, and decreased vision; small round blue cells with Flexner-Wintersteiner rosettes on biopsy

correlates.name: Rhabdomyolysis
correlates.pathophysiology: Skeletal muscle breakdown releases myoglobin, risking tubular obstruction and AKI
correlates.treatment: Aggressive isotonic IV fluids; treat the underlying cause
correlates.presentation: Bodybuilder after intense exercise has muscle pain, tea-colored urine, CK >10,000, and acute kidney injury

correlates.name: Rocky Mountain Spotted Fever
correlates.pathophysiology: Rickettsia rickettsii invades vascular endothelium causing systemic vasculitis; transmitted by Dermacentor ticks
correlates.treatment: Empiric doxycycline (even in children) without delay; high mortality if untreated
correlates.presentation: Hiker in the southeastern US in summer with fever, headache, and a petechial/maculopapular rash starting at the wrists/ankles and spreading centrally to involve palms and soles

correlates.name: Rosacea
correlates.pathophysiology: Innate immune dysregulation with elevated cathelicidin and possible Demodex mite role
correlates.treatment: Trigger avoidance, topical metronidazole/ivermectin, oral doxycycline
correlates.presentation: 40F with central facial erythema, telangiectasias, and inflammatory papules without comedones; flushes with alcohol

correlates.name: Sarcoidosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Th1-driven non-caseating granulomatous inflammation of unknown cause
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids first-line; methotrexate or hydroxychloroquine
correlates.presentation: 30F African-American with bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy, erythema nodosum, and non-caseating granulomas on biopsy

correlates.name: Scurvy
correlates.pathophysiology: Vitamin C deficiency impairs collagen synthesis (proline/lysine hydroxylation)
correlates.treatment: Oral vitamin C replacement
correlates.presentation: Elderly homebound patient with perifollicular hemorrhage, 'corkscrew hairs', swollen bleeding gums, poor wound healing, and ecchymoses

correlates.name: Sebaceous Hyperplasia
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign enlargement of sebaceous glands with age; can mimic basal cell carcinoma
correlates.treatment: Observation; electrodessication, laser, or topical retinoids for cosmesis
correlates.presentation: 50M with multiple yellow-white umbilicated 'donut-shaped' papules on the forehead, cheeks, and nose that increase with age

correlates.name: Seborrheic Dermatitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Inflammatory response to Malassezia yeast in sebum-rich skin; severe forms suggest HIV or Parkinson disease
correlates.treatment: Selenium sulfide or zinc pyrithione shampoo; ketoconazole; low-potency steroids for face
correlates.presentation: 39M with chronic ill-defined greasy yellow scaly patches on the scalp, eyebrows, nasolabial folds, and central chest; consider HIV testing if new onset and severe

correlates.name: Seborrheic Keratosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign basaloid keratinocyte hyperplasia with horn cysts; activating FGFR3 mutations
correlates.treatment: Benign; cryotherapy or curettage if cosmetically desired
correlates.presentation: 70M with multiple waxy 'stuck-on' brown papules on the trunk and face

correlates.name: Sickle cell disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Glutamate-to-valine mutation in beta-globin; HbS polymerizes under hypoxia/acidosis
correlates.treatment: Hydroxyurea; hydration, analgesia, vaccination against encapsulated organisms
correlates.presentation: African-American child with painful vaso-occlusive crises, dactylitis, and hemoglobin SS on electrophoresis

correlates.name: Sideroblastic anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Defective protoporphyrin synthesis causes iron to accumulate in mitochondria as ringed sideroblasts
correlates.treatment: Pyridoxine (vitamin B6); remove offending agent (alcohol, isoniazid)
correlates.presentation: Alcoholic with microcytic anemia, high serum iron and ferritin, and ringed sideroblasts on marrow biopsy

correlates.name: Sister Mary Joseph Nodule
correlates.pathophysiology: Periumbilical metastatic nodule from intra-abdominal malignancy (most often gastric or pancreatic adenocarcinoma)
correlates.treatment: Workup and treat the underlying primary malignancy; generally poor prognosis
correlates.presentation: 65M with weight loss and a firm umbilical nodule on exam; CT reveals an underlying pancreatic head adenocarcinoma

correlates.name: Spitz Nevus
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign melanocytic proliferation that can histologically mimic melanoma; previously called 'juvenile melanoma'
correlates.treatment: Excisional biopsy with histologic confirmation; close follow-up
correlates.presentation: 8F with a rapidly enlarging pink-tan dome-shaped papule on the face for 4 months; histology required to distinguish from melanoma

correlates.name: Splenic Sequestration Crisis
correlates.pathophysiology: Sickle cell spleen suddenly traps a large blood volume causing hypovolemic shock
correlates.treatment: Urgent transfusion; volume resuscitation; splenectomy if recurrent
correlates.presentation: Child with sickle cell disease has sudden hypotension, severe anemia, and a rapidly enlarging spleen

correlates.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
correlates.pathophysiology: UV-induced p53 mutations drive malignant keratinocytes invading through the basement membrane
correlates.treatment: Excision or Mohs surgery; cemiplimab for advanced disease
correlates.presentation: 70M with chronic sun exposure has a scaly hyperkeratotic ulcerated nodule on the lower lip

correlates.name: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: S. aureus exfoliative toxins cleave desmoglein-1 in the granular layer causing intraepidermal separation
correlates.treatment: Anti-staphylococcal IV antibiotics and supportive fluid care
correlates.presentation: Toddler with diffuse desquamating erythema and positive Nikolsky sign after staph infection; mucosa spared

correlates.name: Staphylococcal Scalded Skin Syndrome (SSSS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Hematogenous spread of S. aureus exfoliative toxin (ETA/ETB) cleaves desmoglein 1 in superficial epidermis
correlates.treatment: IV anti-staphylococcal antibiotics (nafcillin/oxacillin); supportive fluids and wound care
correlates.presentation: Toddler with fever, irritability, erythroderma, and flaccid bullae sparing mucous membranes; positive Nikolsky sign with sloughing of large sheets of epidermis

correlates.name: Stasis Dermatitis
correlates.pathophysiology: Chronic venous hypertension causes capillary leak and hemosiderin deposition
correlates.treatment: Compression therapy (cornerstone), leg elevation, topical steroids
correlates.presentation: 70F with chronic venous insufficiency has bilateral lower-leg edema, hyperpigmentation, and itchy eczematous patches

correlates.name: Stevens-Johnson Syndrome / Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis
correlates.pathophysiology: Type IV cytotoxic T-cell drug reaction causing widespread keratinocyte apoptosis and epidermal necrosis
correlates.treatment: Stop the offending drug immediately; burn-unit-level supportive care
correlates.presentation: Patient 1-3 weeks after starting a sulfonamide has painful mucosal erosions and >10% epidermal detachment

correlates.name: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Somatic GNAQ mutation causing V1 port wine stain and leptomeningeal angiomas
correlates.treatment: Anticonvulsants, pulsed-dye laser, IOP control for glaucoma
correlates.presentation: Infant with a port-wine stain in the V1 distribution has seizures, glaucoma, and 'tram-track' intracranial calcifications

correlates.name: Subacute combined degeneration
correlates.pathophysiology: B12 deficiency raises methylmalonic acid, damaging dorsal columns and lateral corticospinal tracts
correlates.treatment: B12 replacement; deficits may be irreversible if delayed
correlates.presentation: Elderly patient with B12 deficiency has loss of vibration and proprioception, lateral CST signs, and dementia

correlates.name: Syringoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign adenoma of eccrine sweat ducts
correlates.treatment: Cosmetic excision, electrodessication, or laser
correlates.presentation: 30F with multiple 1-2mm flesh-colored papules clustered on the lower eyelids; benign and asymptomatic

correlates.name: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
correlates.pathophysiology: Loss of self-tolerance with antinuclear autoantibodies and immune-complex deposition
correlates.treatment: Photoprotection, hydroxychloroquine, corticosteroids, immunosuppressants
correlates.presentation: 30F African-American with malar rash, oral ulcers, arthritis, and serositis; ANA and anti-dsDNA positive

correlates.name: Systemic Sclerosis (Scleroderma)
correlates.pathophysiology: Fibroblast overproduction of collagen sclerosing skin and internal organs
correlates.treatment: Immunosuppressants; ACE inhibitors for scleroderma renal crisis
correlates.presentation: 40F with skin thickening, sclerodactyly, Raynaud phenomenon, and esophageal dysmotility; anti-Scl-70 positive

correlates.name: Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP)
correlates.pathophysiology: ADAMTS13 deficiency leaves large vWF multimers that trap platelets into microthrombi
correlates.treatment: Plasma exchange; avoid platelet transfusion
correlates.presentation: 30F with fever, neurologic changes, thrombocytopenia, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, and renal failure; ADAMTS13 deficient

correlates.name: Tinea Corporis
correlates.pathophysiology: Dermatophyte infection of glabrous skin (most often Trichophyton rubrum) by autoinoculation or animal/soil contact
correlates.treatment: Topical antifungals (terbinafine, azoles); oral therapy for extensive disease
correlates.presentation: 30F dog owner with annular erythematous scaly plaques on the arm with active raised borders and central clearing; KOH shows branching septate hyphae

correlates.name: Tinea Cruris (Jock Itch)
correlates.pathophysiology: Dermatophyte infection of the inguinal region, most often Trichophyton rubrum; favors moist warm folds
correlates.treatment: Topical antifungals; keep area dry; treat tinea pedis to prevent reinfection
correlates.presentation: 20M postpubertal athlete with bilateral annular plaques on the medial thighs and groin sparing the scrotum/penis; KOH positive

correlates.name: Tinea Versicolor
correlates.pathophysiology: Overgrowth of Malassezia furfur (hyphal form) producing azelaic acid that inhibits melanocytes
correlates.treatment: Selenium sulfide shampoo, ketoconazole; pigment changes resolve over months
correlates.presentation: 22M with hypopigmented and hyperpigmented sharply marginated scaly macules on the upper trunk that became apparent with summer tanning; KOH shows 'spaghetti and meatballs'

correlates.name: Toxic Shock Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Superantigen-driven massive T-cell activation, cytokine storm, and capillary leak
correlates.treatment: Remove source; clindamycin plus vancomycin; fluids and vasopressors
correlates.presentation: Menstruating woman using tampons has high fever, hypotension, diffuse macular rash, and later desquamation

correlates.name: Transfusion-associated circulatory overload (TACO)
correlates.pathophysiology: Volume overload causes cardiogenic pulmonary edema with elevated CVP/PCWP
correlates.treatment: Diuretics (furosemide); slow infusion rate
correlates.presentation: Elderly patient receiving rapid transfusion develops hypertension, dyspnea, and pulmonary edema within 6 hours

correlates.name: Transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease (TA-GVHD)
correlates.pathophysiology: Donor T cells engraft in an immunocompromised host and attack host tissues
correlates.treatment: Prevented by irradiation of blood products; >90% fatal once established
correlates.presentation: Immunocompromised patient 1-2 weeks post-transfusion has fever, rash, diarrhea, and pancytopenia from engrafting donor T cells

correlates.name: Transfusion-related acute lung injury (TRALI)
correlates.pathophysiology: Donor anti-neutrophil antibodies activate recipient pulmonary neutrophils; non-cardiogenic edema with normal CVP
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; avoid implicated donors
correlates.presentation: Patient develops acute bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and hypoxia within 6 hours of transfusion; donor anti-HLA antibodies implicated

correlates.name: Transient Erythroblastopenia of Childhood (TEC)
correlates.pathophysiology: Transient autoimmune suppression of erythroid precursors, typically 2-3 months after a viral illness; reticulocytopenia with normocytic anemia
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; spontaneous recovery in 1-2 months; transfusion only if symptomatic
correlates.presentation: Previously healthy 1-3 year old with slowly developing pallor, normocytic anemia (Hb 6-8), low reticulocytes, but normal WBC and platelets with no organomegaly or bone pain

correlates.name: Trench Foot (Immersion Foot)
correlates.pathophysiology: Prolonged wet, non-freezing exposure causes neurovascular injury without freezing
correlates.treatment: Elevation; dry, loose dressing; late debridement
correlates.presentation: Soldier after prolonged cold-wet exposure has macerated, painful, swollen feet with skin discoloration

correlates.name: Trichoepithelioma
correlates.pathophysiology: Benign tumor of hair follicle germ cells; multiple lesions can be inherited (autosomal dominant)
correlates.treatment: Excision, electrodessication, or laser for cosmesis
correlates.presentation: Young adult with multiple pink to skin-colored papules clustered around the nose and central face appearing at puberty; can resemble basal cell carcinoma

correlates.name: Trousseau Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Occult malignancy releases procoagulants causing migratory thrombophlebitis
correlates.treatment: Anticoagulation and treat underlying cancer
correlates.presentation: Patient with occult pancreatic adenocarcinoma has migratory superficial thrombophlebitis at different sites

correlates.name: Tumor lysis syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Massive tumor cell death releases uric acid, potassium, and phosphate causing metabolic derangement
correlates.treatment: Aggressive hydration plus allopurinol or rasburicase
correlates.presentation: Patient 12-72 hours after starting chemotherapy for high-grade lymphoma has hyperkalemia, hyperphosphatemia, hyperuricemia, hypocalcemia, and AKI

correlates.name: Uremic Platelet Dysfunction
correlates.pathophysiology: Retained nitrogenous waste products impair platelet aggregation, adhesion, and platelet-endothelium interaction
correlates.treatment: Dialysis; desmopressin (DDAVP) for acute bleeding; cryoprecipitate; conjugated estrogens
correlates.presentation: Patient with chronic kidney disease has mucocutaneous bleeding and prolonged bleeding time despite a normal platelet count and normal PT/PTT

correlates.name: Urticaria
correlates.pathophysiology: Type I IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation causing histamine-driven dermal edema
correlates.treatment: Antihistamines; identify and avoid trigger
correlates.presentation: 20F has transient pruritic raised wheals lasting <24 hours after eating shellfish; IgE-mediated

correlates.name: Vitamin K Deficiency Bleeding
correlates.pathophysiology: Lack of vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation of factors II, VII, IX, X and proteins C and S impairs both intrinsic and extrinsic clotting
correlates.treatment: Vitamin K replacement (oral or parenteral); FFP for acute bleeding
correlates.presentation: Adult on prolonged antibiotics or with malabsorption (cystic fibrosis, pancreatic insufficiency) develops prolonged PT and PTT with normal platelet count and bleeding time

correlates.name: Vitiligo
correlates.pathophysiology: T-cell-mediated autoimmune destruction of melanocytes producing depigmented patches
correlates.treatment: Topical corticosteroids, calcineurin inhibitors, narrowband UVB phototherapy
correlates.presentation: 30M with well-demarcated depigmented patches on the hands and face; autoimmune melanocyte destruction

correlates.name: von Willebrand Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: vWF deficiency impairs platelet adhesion and destabilizes factor VIII (double hit)
correlates.treatment: Desmopressin (DDAVP)
correlates.presentation: Adolescent with easy bruising, epistaxis, and heavy menses; prolonged bleeding time, normal platelet count, low vWF

correlates.name: Warfarin-Induced Skin Necrosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Rapid protein C drop on starting warfarin causes transient hypercoagulable microthrombosis
correlates.treatment: Bridge with heparin when initiating warfarin
correlates.presentation: Patient with protein C deficiency develops skin necrosis on the breast or thigh 3-10 days after starting warfarin

correlates.name: Waterhouse-Friderichsen Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Bilateral adrenal hemorrhage from DIC during meningococcemia
correlates.treatment: Emergent corticosteroids and antibiotics for the sepsis
correlates.presentation: Child with meningococcal sepsis develops adrenal hemorrhage, refractory shock, and DIC

correlates.name: Wilms Tumor (Nephroblastoma)
correlates.pathophysiology: Childhood embryonal renal malignancy with blastemal, stromal, and epithelial elements; associated with WT1/WT2 mutations (WAGR, Denys-Drash, Beckwith-Wiedemann)
correlates.treatment: Nephrectomy plus chemotherapy; radiation for higher stages; >90% cure rate
correlates.presentation: Child age 2-5 with an asymptomatic unilateral abdominal mass that does not cross the midline, hypertension, and painless hematuria

correlates.name: Factor VII Deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: Deficiency of factor VII, the only factor unique to the extrinsic pathway, impairs initiation of coagulation
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with bleeding and an isolated prolonged PT/INR while the aPTT remains normal
correlates.treatment: Recombinant factor VIIa or fresh frozen plasma

correlates.name: Factor XI Deficiency (Hemophilia C)
correlates.pathophysiology: Deficiency of intrinsic-pathway factor XI impairs amplification of thrombin generation; common in Ashkenazi Jews
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with post-surgical or post-traumatic bleeding and an isolated prolonged aPTT with a normal PT
correlates.treatment: Fresh frozen plasma or factor XI concentrate

correlates.name: IV Iron Infusion Reaction
correlates.pathophysiology: Parenteral iron, especially high-molecular-weight iron dextran, can trigger an anaphylactoid hypersensitivity reaction
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with flushing, dizziness, hypotension, and dyspnea during an IV iron dextran infusion
correlates.treatment: Stop infusion and treat anaphylaxis; give a test dose with iron dextran

correlates.name: Folate Masking of Vitamin B12 Deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: Folic acid corrects the megaloblastic anemia of B12 deficiency but does not halt impaired myelin synthesis, allowing neurologic damage to progress
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with resolving anemia after folate supplementation but progressive paresthesias, ataxia, and neuropsychiatric changes
correlates.treatment: Confirm normal B12 before folate monotherapy; replace B12

correlates.name: Erythropoiesis-Stimulating Agent Thrombotic Toxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: ESAs raise hemoglobin and blood viscosity; overshooting target hemoglobin increases thrombotic and cardiovascular risk
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with new hypertension and a thrombotic event (MI, stroke, VTE, or thrombosed access) after escalating ESA therapy
correlates.treatment: Use lowest effective ESA dose targeting Hb 10-11 g/dL; monitor BP

correlates.name: ESA-Induced Pure Red Cell Aplasia
correlates.pathophysiology: Neutralizing anti-erythropoietin antibodies against the ESA cross-react with endogenous EPO, abolishing erythropoiesis
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with sudden transfusion-dependent anemia and a collapsed reticulocyte count after months of subcutaneous epoetin alfa for CKD
correlates.treatment: Discontinue all ESAs (contraindicated); supportive transfusion

correlates.name: Hydroxyurea Myelosuppression
correlates.pathophysiology: Hydroxyurea inhibits ribonucleotide reductase and suppresses the marrow, making myelosuppression the dose-limiting toxicity
correlates.presentation: Patient with sickle cell disease on hydroxyurea presents with neutropenia (and possible thrombocytopenia) on routine CBC during dose titration
correlates.treatment: Hold or dose-reduce hydroxyurea; monitor CBC with differential

correlates.name: Hairy Cell Leukemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Indolent neoplasm of mature B cells with cytoplasmic 'hairy' projections, classically TRAP-positive
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as an older man with massive splenomegaly and a 'dry tap' on bone marrow aspiration due to marrow fibrosis
correlates.treatment: Cladribine (purine analog); excellent prognosis

correlates.name: Polycythemia Vera
correlates.pathophysiology: JAK2-driven myeloproliferative neoplasm with clonal proliferation of myeloid cells and markedly increased red cell mass
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with pruritus after a warm shower, plethora, headache, and an elevated red cell mass with basophilia
correlates.treatment: Therapeutic phlebotomy (plus hydroxyurea/aspirin)

correlates.name: Essential Thrombocythemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Myeloproliferative neoplasm marked by clonal proliferation with markedly increased platelets
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with a markedly elevated platelet count found on routine labs, with thrombosis or paradoxical bleeding
correlates.treatment: Hydroxyurea; aspirin

correlates.name: Primary Myelofibrosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Myeloproliferative neoplasm in which the bone marrow is progressively replaced by fibrosis
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with massive splenomegaly, a leukoerythroblastic smear with teardrop cells, and a dry tap on aspiration
correlates.treatment: JAK inhibitor (ruxolitinib); supportive care

correlates.name: Acute Megakaryoblastic Leukemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Rare AML subtype of megakaryoblast lineage strongly associated with Down syndrome in children under age 5
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a child under 5 with Down syndrome with fatigue, bruising, and marrow blasts
correlates.treatment: AML-directed chemotherapy

correlates.name: Marginal Zone / MALT Lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Indolent B-cell lymphoma arising in chronically inflamed mucosa, classically triggered by H. pylori, Sjogren, or Hashimoto
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with epigastric pain and a low-grade gastric B-cell lymphoma with H. pylori on biopsy
correlates.treatment: H. pylori eradication (antibiotics plus PPI)

correlates.name: Adult T-cell Leukemia/Lymphoma (ATLL)
correlates.pathophysiology: Aggressive mature T-cell malignancy caused by the HTLV-1 retrovirus (endemic to Japan and the Caribbean)
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with skin lesions, lymphadenopathy, hypercalcemia with lytic bone lesions, and 'flower cells' on smear
correlates.treatment: Multiagent chemotherapy (poor prognosis)

correlates.name: Mycosis Fungoides
correlates.pathophysiology: Indolent skin-homing CD4+ T-cell lymphoma with epidermal Pautrier microabscesses
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with progressive skin patches, plaques, and tumors, with CD4+ T cells bearing cerebriform nuclei
correlates.treatment: Skin-directed therapy (topical steroids, phototherapy)

correlates.name: Sezary Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Leukemic, blood-involving phase of mycosis fungoides (CD4+ T-cell lymphoma)
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with diffuse erythroderma and circulating Sezary cells with cerebriform nuclei
correlates.treatment: Systemic therapy (e.g., extracorporeal photopheresis)

correlates.name: Anaplastic Large Cell Lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Aggressive CD30-positive T-cell lymphoma, frequently ALK-positive in younger patients
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a younger patient with lymphadenopathy and CD30+/ALK+ large anaplastic cells on biopsy
correlates.treatment: Brentuximab vedotin-based chemotherapy

correlates.name: Primary CNS Lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Almost always a B-cell DLBCL of the CNS, strongly associated with HIV and EBV
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as an immunocompromised patient with a single ring-enhancing lesion crossing the corpus callosum
correlates.treatment: High-dose methotrexate

correlates.name: Nodular Lymphocyte-Predominant Hodgkin Lymphoma
correlates.pathophysiology: Non-classical Hodgkin lymphoma whose 'popcorn' (L&H) cell is CD20+/CD45+ but CD15-/CD30- (inverse of classical HL)
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with isolated indolent lymphadenopathy and popcorn cells on biopsy, with an excellent prognosis
correlates.treatment: Rituximab-based therapy or radiation

correlates.name: Monoclonal Gammopathy of Undetermined Significance (MGUS)
correlates.pathophysiology: Premalignant plasma cell dyscrasia with M-protein <3 g/dL, <10% marrow plasma cells, and no end-organ damage
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with an incidental serum M-spike on electrophoresis without CRAB features
correlates.treatment: Surveillance (progresses to myeloma ~1% per year)

correlates.name: Smoldering Multiple Myeloma
correlates.pathophysiology: Intermediate plasma cell dyscrasia with M-protein >=3 g/dL or 10-60% marrow plasma cells but no end-organ damage
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with a high M-spike and increased marrow plasma cells but no CRAB findings
correlates.treatment: Close observation

correlates.name: Waldenstrom Macroglobulinemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Lymphoplasmacytic lymphoma producing monoclonal IgM (usually MYD88 L265P mutated) without lytic bone lesions
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with hyperviscosity (visual changes, mucosal bleeding, neurologic symptoms) and peripheral neuropathy with a high IgM
correlates.treatment: Plasmapheresis for hyperviscosity, then a BTK inhibitor (ibrutinib)

correlates.name: Plasma Cell Leukemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Aggressive plasma cell neoplasm with high M-protein and circulating plasma cells exceeding 2 x 10^9/L
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with widely disseminated disease and circulating malignant plasma cells on peripheral smear
correlates.treatment: Aggressive multiagent chemotherapy

correlates.name: AL Amyloidosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Misfolded monoclonal light chains form beta-pleated sheets depositing in tissues, staining Congo red with apple-green birefringence
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with macroglossia, periorbital 'raccoon eyes' purpura, restrictive cardiomyopathy with low-voltage ECG, and nephrotic-range proteinuria
correlates.treatment: Plasma cell-directed therapy (e.g., bortezomib-based)

correlates.name: Doxorubicin (Anthracycline) Cardiotoxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: Anthracyclines generate iron-dependent oxygen free radicals causing cumulative, dose-related irreversible cardiac myocyte injury
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with progressive dyspnea, fatigue, and edema after cumulative doxorubicin, with echo showing reduced LVEF and dilated cardiomyopathy
correlates.treatment: Limit cumulative dose and monitor LVEF; dexrazoxane cardioprotection

correlates.name: Cyclophosphamide/Ifosfamide Hemorrhagic Cystitis
correlates.pathophysiology: The urotoxic metabolite acrolein is excreted in urine and is directly toxic to bladder epithelium
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with gross hematuria, dysuria, and suprapubic pain during or after cyclophosphamide or ifosfamide therapy
correlates.treatment: Vigorous hydration plus mesna, which inactivates acrolein in the urine

correlates.name: Cisplatin Nephrotoxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: Cisplatin accumulates in and directly damages renal proximal tubular epithelial cells; the dose-limiting toxicity
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with rising serum creatinine and electrolyte wasting (Mg, K) after cisplatin chemotherapy
correlates.treatment: Vigorous saline diuresis; amifostine; consider carboplatin

correlates.name: Cisplatin Ototoxicity and Neuropathy
correlates.pathophysiology: Cisplatin causes cumulative damage to cochlear hair cells and dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with high-frequency hearing loss, tinnitus, and a stocking-glove sensory neuropathy following cisplatin therapy
correlates.treatment: Audiometric and neurologic monitoring with dose reduction

correlates.name: Oxaliplatin Cold-Induced Neuropathy
correlates.pathophysiology: Oxaliplatin produces an acute, cold-triggered sensory neuropathy plus a delayed cumulative dorsal root ganglion neuropathy
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with paresthesias of the hands, feet, and perioral region triggered by cold exposure shortly after a FOLFOX infusion
correlates.treatment: Avoid cold exposure; dose reduction for progressive neuropathy

correlates.name: Busulfan Pulmonary Fibrosis
correlates.pathophysiology: The alkylating agent busulfan causes chronic pulmonary epithelial injury leading to interstitial fibrosis ('busulfan lung')
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with progressive dyspnea and nonproductive cough with diffuse interstitial infiltrates months after busulfan therapy
correlates.treatment: Discontinue the agent; supportive care and glucocorticoids

correlates.name: Methotrexate Toxicity (Mucositis/Myelosuppression)
correlates.pathophysiology: Methotrexate inhibits dihydrofolate reductase, depleting reduced folate needed for DNA synthesis in marrow and GI mucosa
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with painful oral mucositis, stomatitis, and pancytopenia following high-dose methotrexate
correlates.treatment: Leucovorin (folinic acid) rescue

correlates.name: Fluorouracil/Capecitabine Hand-Foot Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Fluoropyrimidine toxicity to palmar and plantar epithelium causes palmar-plantar erythrodysesthesia, especially with capecitabine
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with painful erythema, swelling, and desquamation of the palms and soles during capecitabine or 5-FU therapy
correlates.treatment: Dose reduction or interruption; supportive skin care

correlates.name: Fluorouracil Coronary Vasospasm
correlates.pathophysiology: 5-FU can induce coronary artery vasospasm leading to myocardial ischemia
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with anginal chest pain (and possible arrhythmia) during a 5-FU infusion
correlates.treatment: Discontinue 5-FU; nitrates or calcium channel blockers

correlates.name: Cytarabine Cerebellar Neurotoxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: High-dose cytarabine distributes to the CNS and is toxic to cerebellar neurons
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with ataxia, dysarthria, and nystagmus after high-dose cytarabine therapy
correlates.treatment: Discontinue or reduce dose; supportive care

correlates.name: Vincristine Peripheral Neuropathy
correlates.pathophysiology: Vincristine disrupts axonal microtubules in peripheral and autonomic nerves; the dose-limiting toxicity
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with pins-and-needles paresthesias, motor weakness, and severe constipation following a vincristine-containing regimen
correlates.treatment: Dose reduction; bowel regimen; never give intrathecally

correlates.name: Irinotecan-Induced Diarrhea
correlates.pathophysiology: Irinotecan causes acute cholinergic diarrhea and delayed severe diarrhea, worsened by deficient UGT1A1 metabolism of active SN-38
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with severe watery diarrhea and dehydration after irinotecan, either acute (cholinergic) or delayed
correlates.treatment: Atropine for acute diarrhea; loperamide for delayed diarrhea

correlates.name: Bleomycin Pulmonary Fibrosis
correlates.pathophysiology: A bleomycin-DNA-iron complex generates free radicals that damage lung tissue, producing interstitial fibrosis
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with progressive dyspnea, dry cough, and bibasilar crackles after BEP therapy for testicular cancer
correlates.treatment: Discontinue bleomycin; monitor pulmonary function; glucocorticoids

correlates.name: Trastuzumab Cardiotoxicity
correlates.pathophysiology: HER2 blockade in cardiomyocytes impairs myocardial function; risk is highest when combined with anthracyclines
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with declining LVEF and signs of heart failure during HER2-targeted therapy, often after prior doxorubicin
correlates.treatment: Monitor LVEF; hold the drug and manage heart failure; avoid concurrent anthracycline

correlates.name: Warfarin Supratherapeutic INR Bleeding
correlates.pathophysiology: Excess VKORC1 inhibition depletes vitamin K-dependent factors II, VII, IX, X, raising bleeding risk sharply once INR exceeds 4
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with an INR of 11 and active bleeding while on chronic warfarin therapy
correlates.treatment: Hold warfarin; oral vitamin K; IV vitamin K plus 4-factor PCC (or FFP) for serious bleeding

correlates.name: Fetal Warfarin Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Warfarin crosses the placenta and disrupts vitamin K-dependent gamma-carboxylation during fetal development
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a newborn whose mother took warfarin in the first trimester, with nasal hypoplasia and stippled epiphyses
correlates.treatment: Prevent by avoiding warfarin in pregnancy; substitute LMWH or heparin

correlates.name: Warfarin Purple Toe Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Early warfarin therapy may release atheromatous cholesterol microemboli into the distal circulation
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with painful purple/blue discoloration of the toes weeks after starting warfarin
correlates.treatment: Discontinue warfarin; supportive care

correlates.name: Heparin Overdose Bleeding
correlates.pathophysiology: Excess unfractionated heparin overaccelerates antithrombin-mediated inactivation of thrombin and factor Xa
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with bleeding and a markedly prolonged aPTT during a heparin infusion
correlates.treatment: Protamine sulfate (ionically binds and neutralizes UFH)

correlates.name: Heparin Resistance
correlates.pathophysiology: Antithrombin deficiency or elevated heparin-binding acute-phase proteins (factor VIII, fibrinogen) blunt heparin's effect
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with failure to reach a therapeutic aPTT despite very high doses of heparin
correlates.treatment: Antithrombin repletion or switch to a non-heparin anticoagulant

correlates.name: Spinal/Epidural Hematoma from Anticoagulation
correlates.pathophysiology: Anticoagulant or antiplatelet therapy at the time of neuraxial anesthesia allows a hematoma to compress the cord or cauda equina
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with back pain, leg weakness, and bowel/bladder dysfunction after spinal anesthesia while anticoagulated
correlates.treatment: Emergent surgical decompression; avoid neuraxial techniques in anticoagulated patients

correlates.name: Heparin-Induced Osteoporosis
correlates.pathophysiology: Long-term unfractionated heparin use reduces bone density
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with fragility fractures after prolonged long-term heparin therapy
correlates.treatment: Discontinue or limit long-term heparin; bone-protective measures

correlates.name: Factor Xa Inhibitor Bleeding
correlates.pathophysiology: DOAC factor Xa inhibitors (rivaroxaban, apixaban) directly block free and clot-bound factor Xa
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with severe gastrointestinal bleeding while taking rivaroxaban or apixaban
correlates.treatment: 4-factor PCC; andexanet alfa (recombinant decoy factor Xa)

correlates.name: Dabigatran Bleeding
correlates.pathophysiology: Dabigatran directly inhibits free and clot-bound thrombin; overanticoagulation or trauma causes bleeding
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with major bleeding while taking dabigatran
correlates.treatment: Idarucizumab, a monoclonal antibody fragment that specifically binds dabigatran

correlates.name: Thrombolytic (tPA) Hemorrhage
correlates.pathophysiology: Fibrinolytics generate plasmin that lyses protective hemostatic plugs and degrades circulating coagulation factors, producing a systemic lytic state
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with sudden severe headache and neurologic decline (intracranial hemorrhage) after alteplase for acute ischemic stroke
correlates.treatment: Stop the fibrinolytic; cryoprecipitate/FFP and supportive care

correlates.name: Streptokinase Hypersensitivity
correlates.pathophysiology: Streptokinase is a bacterial protein, so cross-reacting anti-streptococcal antibodies trigger allergic reactions and neutralize its activity
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with fever, chills, and an allergic reaction after streptokinase, often with prior streptococcal exposure
correlates.treatment: Discontinue streptokinase; supportive/antiallergic therapy; avoid re-exposure

correlates.name: Aspirin-Induced Reye Syndrome
correlates.pathophysiology: Aspirin use in children during a viral illness precipitates mitochondrial injury with hepatic failure and encephalopathy
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a child recovering from a viral illness who develops vomiting, lethargy, and encephalopathy after receiving aspirin
correlates.treatment: Avoid aspirin in children with viral illness; supportive care

correlates.name: Aspirin-Exacerbated Respiratory Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Aspirin's COX inhibition shunts arachidonic acid to leukotrienes, precipitating rhinosinusitis and bronchospasm
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with nasal polyps, urticaria, rhinosinusitis, and bronchospasm shortly after taking aspirin
correlates.treatment: Discontinue and avoid aspirin; treat bronchospasm; consider aspirin desensitization

correlates.name: Ticagrelor-Induced Dyspnea
correlates.pathophysiology: The reversible P2Y12 inhibitor ticagrelor causes dyspnea and bradyarrhythmias in addition to bleeding
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with new-onset dyspnea and bradyarrhythmia after starting ticagrelor
correlates.treatment: Reassurance as dyspnea usually resolves; discontinue if severe

correlates.name: Febrile Non-Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction (FNHTR)
correlates.pathophysiology: Cytokines released from donor leukocytes during storage trigger fever; the most common transfusion reaction, with no hemolysis
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with fever and chills during or shortly after a transfusion, without flank pain, hypotension, or signs of hemolysis
correlates.treatment: Antipyretics; prevent with leukoreduction of products

correlates.name: Anaphylactic Transfusion Reaction
correlates.pathophysiology: Anti-IgA antibodies in an IgA-deficient recipient react against IgA in donor plasma
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with rapid urticaria, bronchospasm, and shock within seconds to minutes of starting a transfusion
correlates.treatment: Stop transfusion; epinephrine; give washed (IgA-depleted) products

correlates.name: Delayed Hemolytic Transfusion Reaction (DHTR)
correlates.pathophysiology: Anamnestic antibody response to minor RBC antigens (Kidd, Kell, Duffy) on re-exposure causes extravascular hemolysis
correlates.presentation: Patient presents days after a transfusion with a falling hemoglobin, low-grade fever, and jaundice from delayed extravascular hemolysis
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; extended RBC phenotype matching for future units

correlates.name: Hydrops Fetalis
correlates.pathophysiology: Severe fetal anemia (Rh-HDFN or alpha-thalassemia Hb Bart's) causes high-output cardiac failure and extramedullary hematopoiesis
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a fetus/newborn with diffuse edema, ascites, pleural and pericardial effusions, and hepatosplenomegaly
correlates.treatment: Intrauterine transfusion; deliver and support; RhoGAM prophylaxis to prevent

correlates.name: Kernicterus
correlates.pathophysiology: Unconjugated bilirubin from hemolytic disease of the newborn crosses the immature blood-brain barrier and deposits in the basal ganglia
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a jaundiced newborn with lethargy, poor feeding, hypotonia, and a high-pitched cry progressing to opisthotonos
correlates.treatment: Phototherapy; exchange transfusion for severe hyperbilirubinemia

correlates.name: Hemoglobin C Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: Glu-to-Lys substitution on the beta-globin chain causes hemoglobin C to crystallize, producing a mild chronic hemolytic anemia
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with a mild hemolytic anemia, target cells, and rod-shaped HbC crystals on the peripheral smear
correlates.treatment: Supportive care

correlates.name: Pyruvate Kinase Deficiency
correlates.pathophysiology: Autosomal recessive deficiency of pyruvate kinase depletes RBC ATP, causing rigid cells and chronic extravascular hemolysis
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a child with chronic hemolytic anemia, jaundice, splenomegaly, and burr cells (echinocytes) on smear
correlates.treatment: Supportive care; splenectomy in severe cases

correlates.name: Warm Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: IgG autoantibodies bind RBCs at body temperature, leading to splenic (extravascular) destruction; linked to SLE, CLL, and methyldopa
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with anemia, jaundice, spherocytes, and a positive direct Coombs test, often with underlying SLE or CLL
correlates.treatment: Corticosteroids; treat underlying cause; rituximab/splenectomy if refractory

correlates.name: Cold Agglutinin Disease
correlates.pathophysiology: IgM autoantibodies bind RBCs in cold peripheral blood and fix complement, causing complement-mediated hemolysis; linked to Mycoplasma and EBV
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with acrocyanosis and hemolysis triggered by cold exposure, often after Mycoplasma pneumonia or infectious mononucleosis
correlates.treatment: Avoid cold exposure; treat underlying infection; rituximab if needed

correlates.name: Pernicious Anemia
correlates.pathophysiology: Autoimmune destruction of gastric parietal cells eliminates intrinsic factor, causing vitamin B12 malabsorption and megaloblastic anemia
correlates.presentation: Patient presents with macrocytic anemia, glossitis, and neurologic symptoms, with anti-intrinsic-factor antibodies and atrophic gastritis
correlates.treatment: Lifelong parenteral (or high-dose oral) vitamin B12

correlates.name: Orotic Aciduria
correlates.pathophysiology: UMP synthase deficiency blocks pyrimidine synthesis, producing a megaloblastic anemia that is NOT corrected by B12 or folate
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a child with megaloblastic anemia and failure to thrive, with orotic acid in the urine but NO hyperammonemia
correlates.treatment: Uridine triacetate

correlates.name: Functional Asplenia (Autosplenectomy)
correlates.pathophysiology: Repeated splenic infarction in sickle cell disease destroys the spleen by age 5-6, eliminating protection against encapsulated organisms
correlates.presentation: Patient presents as a young child with sickle cell disease with Howell-Jolly bodies on smear and overwhelming infection by encapsulated bacteria
correlates.treatment: Daily penicillin prophylaxis until age 5; pneumococcal, Hib, and meningococcal vaccines

dermterms.name: Macule
dermterms.definition: Flat, non-palpable, circumscribed area <1 cm differing from surrounding skin only in color

dermterms.name: Patch
dermterms.definition: Flat, non-palpable, circumscribed area >1 cm differing only in color (essentially a large macule)

dermterms.name: Papule
dermterms.definition: Solid, elevated, circumscribed lesion <1 cm above the skin surface

dermterms.name: Plaque
dermterms.definition: Solid, broadly elevated, flat-topped lesion >1 cm (often a coalescence of papules)

dermterms.name: Nodule
dermterms.definition: Solid, circumscribed, elevated lesion 1-5 cm extending deeper into dermis or subcutis

dermterms.name: Tumor
dermterms.definition: Solid, circumscribed elevated mass >5 cm

dermterms.name: Vesicle
dermterms.definition: Elevated, circumscribed lesion filled with clear serous fluid, <1 cm

dermterms.name: Bulla
dermterms.definition: Elevated, circumscribed lesion filled with clear serous fluid, >1 cm (essentially a large vesicle)

dermterms.name: Pustule
dermterms.definition: Elevated, circumscribed lesion filled with purulent fluid (any size)

dermterms.name: Wheal
dermterms.definition: Transient, elevated, erythematous area of dermal edema (welt or hive)

dermterms.name: Scale
dermterms.definition: Accumulation of loose or adherent desquamated keratin from the stratum corneum
dermterms.example: Silvery scale of psoriasis; seborrheic dermatitis

dermterms.name: Crust
dermterms.definition: Dried serum, blood, or pus overlying damaged skin

dermterms.name: Eschar
dermterms.definition: Type of thick adherent crust indicating underlying skin necrosis
dermterms.example: Anthrax eschar; deep burn; pressure ulcer

dermterms.name: Erosion
dermterms.definition: Superficial depression from loss of epidermis only; heals WITHOUT scarring

dermterms.name: Excoriation
dermterms.definition: Linear erosion caused by scratching or abrasion

dermterms.name: Ulceration
dermterms.definition: Depression from loss of epidermis AND at least part of the dermis; heals WITH scarring
dermterms.example: Venous stasis ulcer; arterial ulcer; pressure ulcer

dermterms.name: Fissure
dermterms.definition: Linear cleavage or crack in the skin extending into the dermis

dermterms.name: Atrophy
dermterms.definition: Thinning of the skin layers — fine wrinkling (epidermal) or surface depression (dermal)

dermterms.name: Lichenification
dermterms.definition: Thickening of the epidermis with accentuation of normal skin markings from chronic rubbing
dermterms.example: Chronic atopic dermatitis; lichen simplex chronicus

dermterms.name: Hypertrophic scar
dermterms.definition: Area of fibrous tissue proliferation that is elevated but confined to the original wound borders
dermterms.example: Post-surgical scar that stays within the incision

dermterms.name: Keloid
dermterms.definition: Excessive fibrous tissue proliferation that extends beyond the original wound borders
dermterms.example: Earlobe or chest keloid (more common in darker skin)

dermterms.name: Xerosis
dermterms.definition: Abnormally dry skin

dermterms.name: Annular
dermterms.definition: Ring-shaped lesion with variation in appearance between the periphery and the center

dermterms.name: Nummular (discoid)
dermterms.definition: Circular or coin-shaped lesion with uniform appearance throughout

dermterms.name: Targetoid
dermterms.definition: Ring-shaped lesion with two distinct concentric zones of differing appearance

dermterms.name: Arcuate
dermterms.definition: Incomplete ring or arc-shaped lesion
dermterms.example: Resolving urticaria; arcuate plaques of mycosis fungoides

dermterms.name: Stellate
dermterms.definition: Lesion with multiple angulated edges resembling a star

dermterms.name: Serpiginous
dermterms.definition: Lesion that wanders as if following the track of a snake

dermterms.name: Reticulate
dermterms.definition: Net-like or lacy arrangement of lesions
dermterms.example: Livedo reticularis; erythema infectiosum body rash

dermterms.name: Grouped (clustered)
dermterms.definition: Multiple lesions positioned immediately adjacent to one another
dermterms.example: Grouped vesicles of HSV; herpes zoster

dermterms.name: Confluent
dermterms.definition: Multiple lesions joining together into a single continuous area

dermterms.name: Discrete
dermterms.definition: Distinct lesions that remain clearly separate from each other

dermterms.name: Geometric
dermterms.definition: Lesions with sharp borders or a pattern suggesting an external object pressed against the skin
dermterms.example: Contact dermatitis from a watch strap or jewelry

dermterms.name: Dermatomal
dermterms.definition: Lesions following the cutaneous distribution of a single spinal nerve root; unilateral and does not cross midline

dermterms.name: Guttate
dermterms.definition: Small drop-like lesions appearing as if applied with a dropper

dermterms.name: Follicular
dermterms.definition: Lesions centered around hair follicles

dermterms.name: Blaschkoid
dermterms.definition: Lesions arranged along Blaschko's lines (developmental skin migration paths)

dermterms.name: Acral
dermterms.definition: Affecting the distal portions of the extremities — hands and feet

dermterms.name: Extensor
dermterms.definition: Affecting extensor surfaces — posterior arms/forearms, anterior thighs/legs, elbows, knees

dermterms.name: Flexural
dermterms.definition: Affecting flexor surfaces — antecubital and popliteal fossae

dermterms.name: Intertriginous
dermterms.definition: Affecting areas where two skin surfaces contact each other — axilla, inguinal, inframammary, intergluteal

dermterms.name: Truncal
dermterms.definition: Affecting the chest, back, and abdomen

dermterms.name: Centrifugal spread
dermterms.definition: Rash that starts on the trunk and spreads outward to the extremities

dermterms.name: Centripetal spread
dermterms.definition: Rash that starts on the extremities and spreads inward toward the trunk

dermterms.name: Cephalocaudal spread
dermterms.definition: Rash that starts on the head and spreads downward toward the feet

dermterms.name: Alopecia
dermterms.definition: Baldness; loss of hair from an area where it normally grows

dermterms.name: Cicatricial alopecia
dermterms.definition: Scarring alopecia in which follicular orifices are destroyed and hair loss is permanent

dermterms.name: Alopecia areata
dermterms.definition: Localized non-scarring autoimmune hair loss occurring in round or oval patches
dermterms.example: Patchy bald spots with characteristic exclamation point hairs

dermterms.name: Telogen effluvium
dermterms.definition: Transient diffuse increased shedding of normal hairs ~3 months after a stressor
dermterms.example: Postpartum or post-illness hair shedding noticed while brushing

dermterms.name: Androgenic alopecia
dermterms.definition: Pattern hair loss — the most common type of progressive hair loss

dermterms.name: Traction alopecia
dermterms.definition: Hair loss caused by chronic pulling tension on the hair; can become permanent if prolonged

dermterms.name: Hirsutism
dermterms.definition: Excess hair growth in women in a male-pattern distribution (face, chest, back)
dermterms.example: Polycystic ovary syndrome; congenital adrenal hyperplasia

dermterms.name: Hypertrichosis
dermterms.definition: Excess hair growth for age, race, and sex in a non-androgenic (non-male-pattern) distribution
dermterms.example: Drug-induced from minoxidil, cyclosporine, or phenytoin

dermterms.name: Exclamation point hairs
dermterms.definition: Short, tapered, easily extracted broken hairs found at the periphery of bald patches

dermterms.name: Chromonychia
dermterms.definition: Any abnormal discoloration of the nail

dermterms.name: Leukonychia
dermterms.definition: White discoloration of the nail (the most common chromonychia)

dermterms.name: Onycholysis
dermterms.definition: Detachment of the nail plate from the distal nail bed

dermterms.name: Nail pitting
dermterms.definition: Small punctate depressions in the nail surface from abnormal keratinization

dermterms.name: Onychorrhexis
dermterms.definition: Distal longitudinal splitting of the nail (brittle nails)

dermterms.name: Onychoschizia
dermterms.definition: Horizontal or lamellar splitting at the free end of the nail
dermterms.example: Frequent water exposure; trauma; nail polish remover

dermterms.name: Trachyonychia
dermterms.definition: Rough, sandpaper-like surface texture of the nails
